title: Use of Myocardial Perfusion Imaging to Guide Prognosis and Management in Older Adults: Is There an Age Limit?
abstract: Background Myocardial perfusion imaging is used to guide risk stratification and revascularization decisions. We aimed to determine whether the prognostic value of ischemia on myocardial perfusion imaging and the association with early revascularization (ER) and outcomes differ across age groups. Methods We included 73 038 patients who underwent single photon emission computed tomography (n=45 252) or positron emission tomography (n=27 786) myocardial perfusion imaging across 20 sites from 2009 to 2024. ER was defined as revascularization within 90 days post-myocardial perfusion imaging. Propensity score-adjusted Cox models evaluated the interaction between age, ischemic burden (myocardial flow reserve for positron emission tomography), and ER for the primary outcome of all-cause death or nonfatal myocardial infarction. Results Median age was 66 years; 45.3% were <65, 31.5% were 65 to 74, 19.1% were 75 to 84, and 4.2% were ≥85. ER was performed in 6.1%, rising to 7.0% in those aged 75 to 84 years and decreasing to 6.5% in those aged ≥85 years. During a median follow-up of 3.7 years, 10 757 deaths/myocardial infarctions occurred. Increasing ischemia was associated with lower event rates after ER versus medical therapy across most age groups, with no significant continuous age-ischemia-ER interaction ( P =0.748). In an exploratory analysis of 3031 patients aged ≥85 years, this association appeared attenuated (hazard ratio for ischemia >10%: 0.90 [0.64-1.26]), although precision was limited, likely reflecting, in part, the small number of patients undergoing ER (n=198). Among positron emission tomography patients, the myocardial flow reserve×ER association did not vary with age (3-way interaction P =0.689). In analyses excluding patients with ER, ischemia remained prognostic in all age groups, though its associated risk declined with advancing age. Conclusions Ischemia remains prognostic across all ages and may help identify candidates who have improved outcomes with ER. In an exploratory analysis, this association appeared attenuated in patients aged ≥85 years, a hypothesis-generating observation. Positron emission tomography-derived myocardial flow reserve may provide complementary physiological information for treatment selection in older adults.

title: Impact of <sup>18</sup>FDG-Avidity and Immunosuppression on Idiopathic and Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
abstract: Background Myocardial 18 fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 FDG)-avidity is frequently seen in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy, as well as a growing "idiopathic 18 FDG-avidity" group of genotype-negative patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis. The prognostic implications of 18 FDG-avidity in patients with and without genetic cardiomyopathy, and the effects of immunosuppression in the latter, remain uncertain. Methods This multicenter, retrospective study included all patients who were referred for both 18 FDG-PET and cardiomyopathy genetic testing. Patients with acute myocarditis, biopsy-proven sarcoidosis, or extracardiac 18 FDG-avidity were excluded. We investigated heart failure (HF) composite (left ventricular assist device, heart transplant, HF hospitalization, or death) and arrhythmia composite (sustained ventricular arrhythmias [ventricular tachycardia/VF], atrioventricular block, or death) outcomes using survival analysis, including Cox proportional hazards modeling and inverse probability of treatment weighting. Results Among 372 patients, 142 (38%) were 18 FDG-avid. The prevalence of genetic cardiomyopathy among 18 FDG-avid patients (12%) was similar to that of 18 FDG-negative patients (18%; P =0.11). Unadjusted, 18 FDG-avidity was associated with an increased risk of HF composite (hazard ratio, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.04-2.75]; P =0.034) and arrhythmia composite (hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.1-2.4]; P =0.014) outcomes compared with 18 FDG-negative patients. However, these associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, nor were there significant differences in 18 FDG-associated risks in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy versus genotype-negative patients. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, immunosuppression of 18 FDG-avid patients (n=49) was not associated with a reduction in HF or arrhythmia composite outcomes compared with those who were not immunosuppressed (n=93). Conclusions Myocardial-only 18 FDG-avidity is not significantly associated with HF or arrhythmia risk in patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis (including those with genetic cardiomyopathy). Immunosuppression therapy does not seem to modify the disease course, suggesting that not all myocardial 18 FDG uptake reflects clinically significant inflammation.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: Background Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m 2 ) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure). Results Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P <0.001). Conclusions Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

title: Lipid Burden and Efficacy of Preventive PCI of Vulnerable Atherosclerotic Coronary Plaques: Post Hoc Analysis From the PREVENT Trial.
abstract: Background Preventive percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of non-flow-limiting lesions (fractional flow reserve >0.80) that are high-risk plaques has emerged as a potential strategy to reduce cardiac events. However, identifying which lesions derive the greatest benefit from preventive PCI compared with optimal medical therapy alone remains challenging. This post hoc analysis evaluates the role of the near-infrared spectroscopy-derived lipid core burden index in identifying high-risk plaques that may benefit from preventive PCI. Methods Among the 1606 patients enrolled in the PREVENT trial (Preventive Coronary Intervention on Stenosis with Functionally Insignificant Vulnerable Plaque) from September 2015 to September 2021, an investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, this post hoc analysis included 598 patients (mean age, 64.1±8.8 years; 27.9% women) comprising 632 lesions with a plaque burden >70% and a minimal lumen area <4 mm 2 by intravascular ultrasound in whom near-infrared spectroscopy evaluation was also performed. Lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was prespecified as having a maximum lipid core burden index over a 4-mm segment >315. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable or progressive angina. Results LRPs were present in 223 patients (37.3%) with 234 lesions. During median follow-up of 5.6 years, primary outcome events occurred more frequently in patients with LRPs than in those with non-LRPs (12.5% versus 4.7%; unadjusted hazard ratio, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.03-4.19; P =0.039) in the overall population. Within the LRP group, preventive PCI was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome compared with optimal medical therapy alone (7.3% vs. 17.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.13-0.41; P <0.001). Conversely, no benefit of preventive PCI was observed in the non-LRP group (5.5% versus 4.2%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.54-1.86; P =0.97). A significant interaction was found between treatment strategy and the presence of LRP ( P interaction <0.001). Conclusions In this post hoc analysis of the PREVENT trial, preventive PCI was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome in patients with near-infrared spectroscopy-defined LRPs, whereas no significant association was observed in those with non-LRPs despite their large plaque burden and small minimal lumen area. These findings suggest the importance of plaque composition, beyond morphological severity alone, in guiding preventive PCI. Registration URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02316886.

title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
abstract: Background Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information. Methods In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed. Results Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P <0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis. Conclusions Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: Background Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. Methods In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Results Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted P <0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). Conclusions In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Thoracic Intermuscular Adiposity, Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction, and Prognosis After Cardiac Surgery.
abstract: Background Body mass index is a widely-used yet imprecise measure of adiposity. Thoracic intermuscular adiposity is reported to be related with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), but their prognostic implications after cardiac surgery are not clear. This study aimed to investigate whether computed tomography-derived thoracic intermuscular adiposity and CMD provide better prognostic information than body mass index in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Methods This study consecutively enrolled 666 patients undergoing elective surgery from 3 centers. Using computed tomography at the T12 vertebral level, we quantified the cross-sectional areas (cm 2 ) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, and intermuscular adipose tissue. Intermuscular fat fraction was calculated as intermuscular adipose tissue/(intermuscular adipose tissue+skeletal muscle)×100%. CMD was defined by a coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance >25. The primary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and rehospitalization for heart failure. Results A total of 63 MACEs (9.5%) occurred during a median 17-month follow-up. Obesity defined by body mass index (10.7% of patients) was not associated with MACE ( P =0.187). Each 1% increase in intermuscular fat fraction was significantly associated with CMD (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.14-1.31]; P <0.001), whereas body mass index showed no such correlation ( P =0.964). CMD independently predicted MACE (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.03; [95% CI: 1.15-3.61]; P = 0.015), whereas intermuscular fat fraction did not ( P =0.516). The annualized MACE rate was significantly higher in patients with CMD (11.0% versus 5.2%, P =0.004). Conclusions Computed tomography-derived intermuscular adiposity correlated strongly with CMD, and preprocedural CMD was associated with a higher risk of MACE after cardiac surgery. External validation and prospective studies are warranted.

title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance. During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination. Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk and may provide complementary information for risk stratification.

title: Association of Obesity With Intracranial Hemodynamic Alterations.
abstract: Obesity increases the risk of stroke and cognitive decline, but its association with intracranial arterial hemodynamics remains unclear. We examined whether obesity score is associated with intracranial signal-intensity gradient, a time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography-derived surrogate of arterial wall shear conditions, and whether this association differs by vascular territory. This cross-sectional study included 5618 adults who underwent comprehensive health screening, including intracranial time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography, in the Republic of Korea between 2012 and 2020. Body mass index was calculated from measured height and weight, and waist circumference was measured by health-screening staff on the same day as brain magnetic resonance angiography. An obesity score was calculated by assigning 1 point each for general and abdominal obesity, yielding scores of 0 (neither), 1 (either), or 2 (both). Arterial SIG and arterial radius were calculated using semiautomated 3-dimensional vessel segmentation. Lower SIG values were interpreted as reflecting reduced arterial wall shear conditions. Multivariable linear regression models assessed the association between obesity score and SIG across 11 intracranial arteries, adjusting for demographics, arterial radius, and cardiometabolic factors. Among 5618 participants (mean [SD] age, 55.9 [8.6] years; 45.2% women), higher obesity score was associated with lower SIG across all intracranial arteries (P value for trend <0.001). In adjusted models, each 1-point increase in obesity score was associated with reduced SIG, including in the basilar artery (B=-0.26 [95% CI, -0.31 to -0.21]). The obesity-related reduction in SIG was greater in the posterior than anterior circulation and persisted after adjustment for arterial radius and cardiometabolic factors. A higher obesity score was associated with reduced intracranial arterial SIG, consistent with adverse time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography-derived flow-related hemodynamic alterations. Greater reductions in the posterior circulation suggest territory-specific vulnerability, which may be associated with early cerebrovascular compromise in the context of obesity.

title: Computed-Tomography Angiography-Based Carotid Plaque-RADS, Recurrent Vascular Events, and the Effect of Colchicine: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial.
abstract: Background The carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) provides a standardized framework for evaluating plaque morphology, but prospective validation remains limited. We investigated the association between computed tomography angiography-based Plaque-RADS categories and subsequent ischemic events in patients with noncardioembolic stroke/transient ischemic attack, from a completed clinical trial of colchicine. Second, we assessed whether the effect of colchicine differed by Plaque-RADS risk classification. Methods We conducted a posthoc observational cohort analysis of 517 participants in the CONVINCE trial (Colchicine for Prevention of Vascular Inflammation in Non-CardioEmbolic Stroke) from 13 European sites. Associations between Plaque-RADS and recurrent ipsilateral stroke, any stroke/transient ischemic attack, and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Plaque-RADS was analyzed as both dichotomized (<3 versus ≥3) and ordinal (per 1-point increase) variables. Treatment effects were assessed by Plaque-RADS classification using interaction and stratified analyses. Results A total of 510 patients (median age, 67.0 years; 72.2% male) with 966 internal carotid arteries were included. Among 321 internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, 12 recurrent ipsilateral strokes, 32 any strokes/transient ischemic attacks, and 37 major adverse cardiovascular events occurred over a median 35.7-month follow-up. Plaque-RADS ≥3 (n=140) was independently associated with recurrent ipsilateral stroke (adjusted hazard ratio, 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55-39.30]; P =0.01), any stroke/transient ischemic attack (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.94 [95% CI, 1.68-9.24]; P <0.01), and major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19-5.34]; P =0.02) after adjustment for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. A significant interaction with colchicine treatment was observed for major adverse cardiovascular events ( P =0.047), with greater benefit among patients with Plaque-RADS scores ≥3 (hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15-0.82]). Conclusions In internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, computed tomography angiography-based carotid Plaque-RADS was associated with recurrent ischemic stroke and cardiovascular events. Importantly, treatment effects of colchicine varied across Plaque-RADS classification (<3 versus ≥3), suggesting that plaque vulnerability assessment may help refine patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy beyond stenosis-based classification. Registration URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02898610.

title: Anatomical determinants of DTI-ALPS: Effects of ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and periventricular deformation.
abstract: The diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is increasingly used as a non-invasive MRI biomarker proposed to reflect glymphatic and perivascular function, yet the anatomical validity and measurement stability of the metric remain incompletely characterised. Using diffusion MRI data from 850 healthy young adults and 150 healthy ageing participants from the Human Connectome Project, I systematically evaluated the influence of region-of-interest (ROI) placement and ventricular anatomy on ALPS measurements. Reference ALPS implementations demonstrated substantial hemispheric variability, with a median left-right difference of 12.5% and marked asymmetry in the underlying numerator and denominator tensor components. A two-stage optimisation framework incorporating fibre-pool alignment, hemispheric symmetry, component stability, and directional purity identified anatomically improved ROI configurations that significantly increased fibre specificity and reduced measurement variability in independent validation cohorts. Despite these improvements, residual hemispheric asymmetry persisted, suggesting an intrinsic anatomical contribution to ALPS variability. In the healthy ageing cohort, ventricular volume emerged as the strongest predictor of ALPS, explaining substantially more variance than chronological age. Voxel-wise deformation-based morphometry demonstrated that lower ALPS values were associated with ventricular and periventricular expansion, while optimisation increased coupling between ALPS and ventricular anatomy. Collectively, these findings indicate that ALPS measurements are strongly influenced by ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and surrounding periventricular tissue architecture. Rather than functioning as a direct measure of glymphatic transport in isolation, ALPS appears to represent a composite anatomical diffusion biomarker shaped by both methodological implementation and underlying neuroanatomy. These results provide a framework for improving methodological standardisation and interpretation of ALPS measurements in future neuroimaging studies.

title: Assessing the reliability of hippocampal single-voxel proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy through intra-class effect decomposition.
abstract: The hippocampus is crucial for learning, memory, and stress regulation, but is vulnerable to influences that compromise its structural and metabolic integrity. Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) enables in vivo quantification of hippocampal neurochemistry, yet the absolute and relative reliability of these measures has rarely been systematically evaluated. We assessed hippocampal metabolite estimates acquired with single-voxel MRS using a semi-adiabatic localization by adiabatic selective refocusing (semi-LASER) sequence at 3 T. Nineteen healthy adults (8 male; mean age = 40.9 ± 16.9 years) underwent four measurements across 2 consecutive days, with one session including an extended acquisition. Absolute reliability was quantified using within-subject coefficients of variation (CVs), and relative reliability was estimated with the Intra-Class Effect Decomposition (ICED) framework, which partitions variance into true-score, day-specific, session-specific, and residual components. Despite good spectral quality and high absolute reliability for several metabolites, relative reliability ranged from poor to good. Good relative reliability was observed only for water-referenced myo-inositol, total choline, and total creatine; no creatine-referenced metabolite reached this threshold. Increasing the number of transients increased signal-to-noise ratio but did not improve relative reliability; only creatine-referenced total N-acetylaspartate showed significant session-specific variance. Thus, high absolute reliability did not necessarily imply high relative reliability. Hippocampal MRS at 3 T may, therefore, be suitable for group-level or mean-level metabolite estimates, but appears less suitable for correlational, biomarker, or other individual-difference applications that require stable between-person differences. Methodological refinement, including improved voxel placement, motion correction, shimming, and quantification pipelines, may improve the relative reliability of hippocampal MRS.

title: Microperimetry Sensitivity Changes at the Functional Transition Zone and at the EZ Margins in X-Linked Retinitis Pigmentosa Treated With Gene Therapy.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the structure-function relationship between the photoreceptor ellipsoid zone (EZ) and functional transition zone (FTZ) in X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (XLRP) eyes treated with gene therapy. Methods In a post-hoc analysis of the Skyline trial, baseline OCT volumes were segmented to generate an en-face map of intact EZ, and after registration with microperimetry (MP) image, the transformed EZ map was used to delineate the EZ margin. FTZ was defined by microperimetry absolute scotomatous points. Non-scotomatous loci adjacent to FTZ, and inside the EZ margin, were analyzed. We quantified the percentage of loci with ≥7 dB sensitivity improvements over 12 months and the average treatment effect (ATE; difference in mean sensitivity change between treated and untreated eyes). Results Twenty-four eyes (12 treated, 12 untreated; seven high-dose, five low-dose) were analyzed. Baseline distance to the EZ margin did not correlate with loci achieving ≥7 dB improvement at month 12 in either dose group. High-dose eyes showed a higher mean percentage of loci with ≥7 dB improvement than untreated eyes for the entire grid, but not on regional analysis. High-dose subjects also showed higher ATE than untreated eyes in all retinal zones. Conclusions High-dose AAV-RPGR gene therapy was associated with improved MP outcomes and greater ATE inside FTZ and intact EZ; however, loci with ≥7 dB improvement did not correlate with baseline EZ margin distance, highlighting challenges in prespecifying localized ≥7 dB changes. Translational relevance Identifying and selecting retinal regions that are likely to show sensitivity improvements may benefit future clinical trials of ocular gene therapy.

title: FFA-SegGPT: A Two-Stage Cross-Modal AI System to Optimize the Clinical Workflow of Diabetic Retinopathy FFA Interpretation.
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study was to develop an interpretable, two-stage artificial intelligence (AI) system (fundus fluorescein angiography [FFA]-SegGPT) designed to optimize the clinical workflow of diabetic retinopathy (DR) FFA interpretation and reduce the risk of factual inaccuracies common in end-to-end models. Methods We developed a cross-modal system that decouples lesion quantification from report generation. A segmentation module first explicitly segments non-perfusion areas (NPAs) and neovascularization (NV). These segmentation maps then serve as visual constraints to guide an evidence-based report generator, ensuring diagnostic text is strictly grounded in detected lesions. Results In a simulated clinical workflow, AI-aided reporting significantly reduced mean interpretation time by 50% (from 8.13 ± 0.47 to 4.09 ± 0.21 minutes, P < 0.001) and improved median report quality (4.0 vs. 3.5, P < 0.001) compared to manual interpretation. Objectively, the model achieved high Dice Similarity Coefficients (NV = 85.35% and NPAs = 86.49%) and maintained high semantic fidelity for report generation (BERTScore = 0.91), with robust generalization demonstrated across three external cohorts. Conclusions FFA-SegGPT enhances both the efficiency and quality of DR diagnostics. By decoupling lesion quantification from report generation, the system provides a transparent, dual-output mechanism that reduces the risk of factual inaccuracies, offering an interpretable workflow to facilitate safe clinical adoption. Translational relevance This interpretable AI system optimizes the clinical workflow of DR by providing verifiable lesion segmentation and automated reporting, potentially reducing clinician workload and standardizing diagnostic quality.

title: Wall-to-Lumen Ratio Estimation in Adaptive Optics Retinal Imaging: Evaluation and Comparison.
abstract: Purpose Retinal arteriolar changes reflect systemic microvascular alterations associated with cardiovascular risk, including hypertension. The retinal arteriolar wall-to-lumen ratio (WLR), obtained by adaptive optics (AO) imaging, is a promising noninvasive biomarker of early vascular damage. Its clinical utility is limited by inter- and intra-grader variability, lack of standardized protocols, and dependence on image quality, boundary definition, and measurement method. Standardized, objective WLR quantification is therefore needed to minimize observer bias and improve reproducibility. Methods We compared point-based and region-based manual WLR estimation using 60 high-resolution AO images from 35 healthy subjects. Two experienced graders performed five point-based measurements per image, yielding one median WLR, followed by manual artery wall and lumen segmentation, yielding one WLR value. Inter-grader variability, method agreement, and sampling-location requirements were evaluated using statistical and Bland-Altman analyses. Results Point-based assessment showed good inter-grader agreement, with a relative mean difference of 4.5% (Wilcoxon test, P < 0.05). Region-based assessment produced significantly lower WLR values than the point-based method (P < 0.01), with relative mean differences of 19.9% and 26.1% for graders A and B, respectively. Inter-grader relative mean difference was 6.2%, comparable to the point-based method. Approximately 10 measurement positions reduced the estimation error to about 5%; fewer positions increased error. Image quality and vessel-border visibility affected WLR variability. Conclusions WLR estimation is influenced by measurement approach, grader experience, image quality, and sampling density. Although region-based assessment is more comprehensive, it is time-consuming. For clinical point-based assessment, at least 10 clearly visible arterial locations are recommended to minimize estimation error. Standardized protocols are essential for reliable WLR quantification. Translational relevance For standardized manual WLR assessment in AO retinal images, we recommend measuring only clearly visible vessel segments, using double-sided measurements whenever possible, avoiding bifurcations, crossings, and adjacent vessels, obtaining ≥12 measurements per artery, excluding the upper and lower deciles, and reporting the median of ≥10 remaining measurements as the final WLR.

title: Unraveling RP1-Associated Retinal Dystrophies: Comprehensive Genetic, Clinical, and Disease Progression Analysis in China.
abstract: Purpose To characterize the clinical manifestations, genetic landscape, and natural history of RP1-associated retinopathy in a Chinese cohort. Methods This longitudinal cohort study enrolled and followed 49 patients with genetically confirmed RP1-associated retinopathy. Phenotyping included visual acuity (VA), visual field, full-field stimulus testing (FST), microperimetry, and multimodal imaging. Genetic analysis and variant interpretation followed American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and Association for Molecular Pathology guidelines. Results The cohort predominantly presented with retinitis pigmentosa (RP, 91.8%) and bilateral involvement, with overall no significant interocular differences in major functional parameters (all P > 0.05). Median symptom onset age was 20 years (interquartile range, 7.25-33.75). On linear regression analysis, earlier onset age (P = 0.024) and longer disease duration (P = 0.019) correlated with worse VA. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated that the median age at which patients reached blindness (>1.3 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution [logMAR]) was 74 years. Quantified decline rates included VA (0.015 logMAR/year) and visual field index (-7.8%/year) in the first decade and FST (0.167 log cd·s/m2/year) and retinal sensitivity (-1.22 dB/year) over two decades. Classic bone-spicule pigmentation was absent in 33.3% of patients. Genetic analysis identified 46 variants; truncating mutations (71.7%) clustered in exon 4, with c.5797C>T as a founder variant (16.3% of alleles). Variants within the upstream one-third of exon 4 were associated with later onset (P = 0.049). Conclusions RP1-associated retinopathy manifests as bilateral, atypical RP with quantifiable, duration-dependent decline and a genotype-phenotype correlation linking upstream exon 4 variants to later onset. Translational relevance Quantified progression rates and genotype-phenotype correlations inform clinical trial endpoints and patient counseling.

title: Spatially Grounded Neurosymbolic AI for Explainable Retinal Disease Classification From OCT Images.
abstract: To develop and evaluate a spatially grounded neurosymbolic AI framework for explainable multilabel retinal disease classification from optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, integrating convolutional neural network (CNN)-based retinal sign extraction, symbolic clinical reasoning, and retinal-layer spatial information. Spectral-domain OCT B-scans were retrospectively collected and classified into ten categories: dry and wet age-related macular degeneration, central serous chorioretinopathy, myopic chorioretinopathy, epiretinal membrane, pseudomacular hole, lamellar macular hole, full-thickness macular hole, diabetic retinopathy, and normal retina. The model combined a CNN backbone with SegFormer-derived retinal-layer maps and mask-guided attention to estimate continuous OCT sign probabilities, which were propagated through expert-defined symbolic rules. Performance was evaluated using multilabel precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Inference was also performed on 402 OCT images from pathologies outside the target taxonomy. Micro-average precision, recall, and F1-score were 0.91, 0.81, and 0.86, respectively; weighted-average values were 0.91, 0.81, and 0.85, and macro-average values were 0.78, 0.71, and 0.74. The micro-average AUC was 0.98. None of the 402 out-of-taxonomy pathological OCT images received a positive Normal-class prediction at the predefined 0.5 threshold. The spatially grounded neurosymbolic framework provided interpretable multilabel OCT classification and showed conservative behavior on pathological images outside the modeled taxonomy. This should not be interpreted as diagnostic recognition of unseen diseases. The framework may support transparent, sign-based, and anatomically grounded AI-assisted OCT interpretation.

title: Time Series Segmentation in Adaptive Optics Ophthalmoscopy With Application to Flicker-Induced Vasodilation.
abstract: Purpose To develop an automated image processing pipeline to segment retinal arterial walls in a series of adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) images, overcoming difficulties related to various quality levels within the series, to accurately evaluate morphometric differences. Methods We first assess the quality of AOO images by deep learning in order to select the best quality image in the sequence. Then, we segment this image by combining deep learning and dedicated active contour models. Finally, we segment the other images of the sequence using the best image segmentation as a regularization exploiting the temporal continuity to compensate for lower quality. Results We applied the proposed method to flicker series, a challenging use-case given the image quality heterogeneity. The quality assessment method achieves a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.86, demonstrating very good agreement with the quality ranking established by the medical expert. The automatic segmentation method results in accurate segmentations with a mean root mean square error of 0.5 pixel and 1.8 pixels for the inner and outer borders of the arterial wall, respectively. This leads to accurate and unbiased estimates of the wall to lumen ratio. Conclusions Our algorithm can be applied as a reliable and useful computer-aided tool to process large time series databases in AOO, and can help experts in longitudinal monitoring applications. Translational relevance For the first time, AOO image series can be processed with low supervision to accurately monitor morphometric changes in retinal vascularization.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

To develop an automated image processing pipeline to segment retinal arterial walls in a series of adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) images, overcoming difficulties related to various quality levels within the series, to accurately evaluate morphometric differences.

Methods

We first assess the quality of AOO images by deep learning in order to select the best quality image in the sequence. Then, we segment this image by combining deep learning and dedicated active contour models. Finally, we segment the other images of the sequence using the best image segmentation as a regularization exploiting the temporal continuity to compensate for lower quality.

Results

We applied the proposed method to flicker series, a challenging use-case given the image quality heterogeneity. The quality assessment method achieves a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.86, demonstrating very good agreement with the quality ranking established by the medical expert. The automatic segmentation method results in accurate segmentations with a mean root mean square error of 0.5 pixel and 1.8 pixels for the inner and outer borders of the arterial wall, respectively. This leads to accurate and unbiased estimates of the wall to lumen ratio.

Conclusions

Our algorithm can be applied as a reliable and useful computer-aided tool to process large time series databases in AOO, and can help experts in longitudinal monitoring applications.

Translational relevance

For the first time, AOO image series can be processed with low supervision to accurately monitor morphometric changes in retinal vascularization.

title: Plasma nucleosome profiling reports on tumor burden and molecular subtypes in small cell lung cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUNDSmall-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis and marked transcriptional heterogeneity that may drive distinct therapeutic vulnerabilities. Clinical translation of molecular subtyping has been limited by restricted access to tumor biopsies, particularly at relapse.METHODSWe applied chromatin immunoprecipitation of cell-free nucleosomes carrying active histone modifications followed by sequencing (cfChIP-seq) to 441 plasma samples from individuals with advanced SCLC, other neuroendocrine carcinomas, or non-SCLC cancers, as well as from healthy controls. Plasma cfChIP-seq profiles were integrated with matched tumor transcriptomes from 73 samples, including 41 time-matched pairs.RESULTScfChIP-seq captured the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of tumor-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA), including SCLC tissue- and cell-of-origin signatures. A quantitative cfChIP-seq-derived SCLC score tracked radiographic tumor burden and was associated with prognosis. Signals at promoters of lineage-defining transcription factor genes, including ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, and ATOH1, correlated strongly with matched tumor RNA expression and supported noninvasive inference of SCLC transcriptional subtypes directly from plasma.CONCLUSIONPlasma cfChIP-seq provides a practical liquid biopsy platform for real-time assessment of tumor burden, tumor state, and molecular subtype in SCLC. These findings support further development of cfChIP-seq for precision monitoring and subtype-informed therapeutic stratification in SCLC.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov NCT02484404, NCT02487095, NCT02769962, NCT03554473, NCT03896503, and NCT02146170.FUNDINGCenter for Cancer Research; Intramural Program of the NCI (ZIA BC 011793); European Research Council (ERC) (Adg no. 101019560 "cfChIP").

title: The Neoadjuvant Window: Serial Assessment of Sarcopenia During Treatment for Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: BackgroundSarcopenia is associated with worse outcomes in pancreatic cancer patients, but longitudinal body composition changes during neoadjuvant therapy remain poorly understood.MethodsA retrospective review identified patients who underwent pancreatectomy, either upfront or after neoadjuvant therapy, for pancreatic adenocarcinoma between 2011 and 2021. Skeletal muscle area, index, and mean attenuation were calculated from CT images throughout the treatment course to assess sarcopenia. Multivariable generalized linear and logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sarcopenia, neoadjuvant therapy, and postoperative outcomes.ResultsA total of 72 patients were included: 32 who underwent neoadjuvant therapy and 40 who underwent upfront surgery. Forty-one (57%) patients had sarcopenia at diagnosis (65% upfront surgery vs 47% neoadjuvant, P = 0.154). Post-neoadjuvant therapy, 15.6% developed and 18.8% resolved sarcopenia. Median skeletal muscle mean attenuation increased by 2.4 HU after neoadjuvant therapy ( P = 0.02). Patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy were more likely to undergo nutrition consultation prior to surgery (61% vs 7%, P = 0.003). Neoadjuvant therapy was also associated with higher postoperative albumin levels (β = 0.244; 95% CI 0.041-0.446). Baseline sarcopenia diagnosed by skeletal muscle area was associated with increased postoperative complications (OR 13.696; 95% CI 2.537-73.921), while neoadjuvant therapy did not significantly impact complications (OR 0.384; 95% CI 0.12-1.226).ConclusionsPatients who completed neoadjuvant therapy and underwent resection did not have increased rates of sarcopenia and were more likely to receive preoperative nutrition consultation and have higher postoperative albumin levels. The neoadjuvant period may represent an opportunity for sarcopenia assessment, nutritional optimization, and multimodal prehabilitation prior to pancreatectomy.

title: Size Under Scrutiny: Preoperative Imaging Size of Mesenteric Deposits Does Not Predict Oncological Outcomes in Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors.
abstract: BackgroundSmall intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SiNETs) are rare tumors with propensity to cause bulky fibrotic mesenteric masses by hematogenous and lymphatic invasion. They exhibit variable oncological behavior and reliable prognostic markers remain elusive. The 8 th edition American Joint Commission on Cancer introduced mesenteric mass ≥2 cm to improve prognostication. The clinical utility in prognostication remains unknown. We reviewed outcomes of resected SiNETs to determine if computed tomography (CT) size is associated with oncological outcomes.MethodsRetrospective review of resected SiNET patients at two tertiary centers with evaluable preoperative CT scans. Measured the largest diameter of the mesenteric mass and the cutoff of 2 cm used to correlate with oncological outcomes.ResultsSeventy-three patients operated for SiNET with preoperative CT were included. The largest mesenteric mass was <2 cm in 28 and ≥2 cm in 45 patients. Cohorts were similar in demographic and clinical characteristics. Median follow-up was 47 months. Overall survival (OS) and progression free survival (PFS) were similar. No significant differences in estimated mean OS (136 vs 139 months, P = 0.981) or median PFS (90 vs 71 months, P = 0.126) for the <2 cm and >2 cm cohorts, respectively. Univariable analysis failed to show an association between mesenteric size as a continuous variable, and at the ≥2 cmcutoff. Age, cardiac comorbidities, and palliative intent surgery were the only factors that correlated with survival.DiscussionMesenteric mass size on preoperative CT was not correlated with oncological outcomes and by itself showed little utility in preoperative decision-making.

title: Preoperative Diagnostic Challenges in Patients Being Evaluated for Resection of Pancreatic Serous Cystadenomas.
abstract: Serous cystadenomas (SCAs) are benign pancreatic cystic neoplasms for which surveillance can be safely discontinued once the diagnosis is established with confidence. However, distinguishing SCAs from premalignant or malignant pancreatic cystic lesions remains challenging despite advances in cross-sectional imaging and endoscopic ultrasound (EUS), resulting in unnecessary pancreatic resection. We performed a retrospective review of all pancreatic resections performed at a single tertiary referral center between January 2010 and December 2022 to identify patients with a final pathological diagnosis of SCA. Demographic, radiographic, operative, and postoperative outcomes were analyzed. Among 556 pancreatic resections, 20 patients (4%) had pathologically confirmed SCAs. The median age was 62 years, 55% were women, and the median cyst size was 3.0 cm. Surgery was performed because malignancy could not be excluded in 40% of patients, concern for a mucinous cystic neoplasm in 35%, and interval cyst growth in 25%. Sixteen patients (80%) underwent preoperative EUS with fine-needle aspiration, but cytology was frequently nondiagnostic and neither confirmed SCA nor reliably excluded a mucinous lesion. Seven patients underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy and 13 underwent distal pancreatectomy. Postoperative morbidity occurred in 50% of patients, including clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula in 30%, with no disease-specific mortality. These findings demonstrate that pancreatic resection for SCAs is driven primarily by persistent diagnostic uncertainty rather than symptoms or malignant potential. Despite contemporary imaging and EUS, confidently differentiating SCAs from premalignant or malignant pancreatic cystic neoplasms remains difficult. Improved diagnostic strategies, including molecular testing and enhanced risk stratification, may reduce unnecessary pancreatic resection while preserving oncologic safety.

title: Delayed Multi-Compartment Traumatic Hernias After Blunt Abdominal Trauma: A Case-Based Review of Diagnosis and Staged Management.
abstract: BackgroundTraumatic diaphragmatic hernias (TDHs) and traumatic abdominal wall hernias (TAWHs) are uncommon sequelae of blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) and may be missed during the initial evaluation. Delayed presentation can occur months to years later, resulting in incarceration, obstruction, or respiratory compromise.Case PresentationA 61-year-old woman presented 1 year after a motor vehicle collision with abdominal pain, nausea, constipation, and dyspnea. Computed tomography demonstrated an incarcerated left diaphragmatic hernia containing colon and omentum, along with a right flank hernia containing ascending colon. Review of prior imaging revealed a flank hematoma and subtle abdominal wall disruption at the time of initial injury. The patient underwent urgent laparoscopic repair of the diaphragmatic hernia followed by elective robotic transabdominal preperitoneal repair of the flank hernia 2 months later.DiscussionThis case illustrates a pattern of delayed multi-compartment traumatic herniation resulting from thoracoabdominal force transmission. Diagnostic delays may occur because of competing priorities during polytrauma management, limitations of initial imaging, and delayed development of herniation, especially when the injuries are subtle. Findings such as rib fractures, pneumothorax, abdominal wall hematoma, and persistent symptoms should prompt continued surveillance.ConclusionDelayed multi-compartment traumatic hernias represent a diagnostic challenge requiring a high index of suspicion, longitudinal surveillance, and individualized management. A staged operative approach based on symptom severity and anatomic location can effectively address differing levels of clinical urgency.

title: Artificial Intelligence Across the Surgical Research Workflow: A Stage-Specific Framework for Benefits, Failure Modes, and Oversight.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, particularly large language models (LLMs), have rapidly integrated into surgical and biomedical research, prompting fundamental questions about their appropriate role. This review presents a stage-specific framework mapping each phase of the surgical research workflow (literature review, data analysis, manuscript preparation, and research synthesis) to the role AI plays, the benefits it provides, the failure modes it introduces, and the oversight it requires. Artificial intelligence-powered query systems are designed to speed literature synthesis across thousands of publications. In data analysis, LLMs paired with statistical environments can perform regression modeling and generate auditable code, while specialized architectures support automated image segmentation and histopathology analysis. Each stage's benefits, however, are matched by characteristic failure modes: LLMs are prone to error and hallucination, reproducibility is threatened by model versioning and run-to-run variability, fabricated citations and paper-mill submissions endanger the integrity of the literature, and over-reliance risks eroding trainee competencies in critical appraisal and biostatistical reasoning. Because these failure modes are stage-specific, governance must be stage-specific as well: the framework pairs each risk with a matched oversight mechanism, and these mechanisms translate into practical implementation recommendations for surgical departments, residency programs, research groups, and journals. The integration of AI into surgical scholarship should be viewed as augmentation rather than replacement, supported by standardized disclosure frameworks, AI literacy in graduate medical education, and institutional governance structures that preserve the integrity of surgical research.

title: Lactation Management in Patients With Cancer: An Evidence-Based Framework for Surgical Practice.
abstract: BackgroundThe coexistence of lactation and cancer care, termed oncolactation , is becoming increasingly common as childbearing is delayed and more women are diagnosed with malignancy during the reproductive years. However, evidence-based guidance regarding breastfeeding during oncologic evaluation and treatment remains fragmented, particularly for surgeons involved in multidisciplinary cancer care.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with a systematic literature search using PubMed/MEDLINE and professional society guidelines (American Society of Breast Surgeons (ASBrS), American College of Radiology (ACR), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed®). Publications addressing surgical management, diagnostic imaging, systemic therapy, radiation therapy, and reproductive counseling in lactating patients with cancer were critically synthesized to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.ResultsMost diagnostic and surgical interventions-including mammography, breast MRI, computed tomography, image-guided biopsy, and general anesthesia-are compatible with continued breastfeeding when appropriate precautions are observed. Cytotoxic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and most targeted or immunotherapeutic agents remain contraindicated because of insufficient safety data or potential infant toxicity. Radiation therapy generally precludes breastfeeding from the treated breast, but permits continued feeding from the contralateral breast. Emerging evidence also supports individualized counseling regarding fertility preservation, future pregnancy, and survivorship.ConclusionsOncolactation should be incorporated into routine surgical oncology practice. Most surgical and diagnostic procedures can be performed without interrupting breastfeeding, whereas systemic therapies require individualized pharmacologic assessment. Integration of evidence-based lactation guidance into multidisciplinary cancer care promotes safe, patient-centered decision-making while maintaining oncologic safety and supporting breastfeeding whenever feasible.

title: Orbital Abscess Complicating Allergic Fungal Rhinosinusitis Due to Streptococcus halichoeri: A Rare Zoonotic Sinonasal Infection.
abstract: Background Secondary bacterial infections complicating allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS) are uncommon but can be serious given the expansile nature of the disease which can thin and erode the bone separating the sinuses from the brain and orbits. Zoonotic pathogens are rarely implicated as pathogens. Case report A 21-year-old African American male with several years of progressive nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and hyposmia, presented emergently with acute left eye pain and swelling, diplopia, afferent pupillary defect and inferior visual field deficit. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute on chronic sinusitis with a left orbital abscess. The patient underwent emergent endoscopic sinus surgery with left orbitotomy and drainage of the orbital abscess. Intraoperative findings, pathology, cultures, and allergy testing were reviewed demonstrating AFRS and a novel zoonotic bacterium, Streptococcus halichoeri . Conclusions This case represents the first otolaryngologic case of S. halichoeri infection, a severe and complicated sinus and orbital infection. It is unclear if the severity of this infection was a consequence of the unusual pathogen, of the long-term thinning of the bone around the orbit, or both. Although AFRS is not considered an infection, secondary bacterial infection may occur and cause severe complications. Early surgical intervention and culture-directed therapy are essential in managing complicated sinonasal diseases.

title: Petrous Apex Mucocele: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundA petrous apex mucocele is a rare benign cystic lesion that can present with symptoms due to pressure on surrounding structures, including the internal carotid artery, Meckel's cave and the fifth and sixth cranial nerves, as well as the cavernous sinus region and inner ear.MethodsA 36-year-old male presented with 8 months of diplopia when looking to the right, a right-sided temporoparietal headache, and paresthesia in the right half of his face. An MRI revealed a 26 × 32 × 37 mm lesion in the right petrous apex. The lesion's signal characteristics were most consistent with a mucocele. We performed an endoscopic endonasal transclival marsupialization and created a wide drainage opening, which we supported by inserting a stent containing mometasone furoate.ResultsThe postoperative course was marked by transient arterial hypertension, which required antihypertensive treatment. Postoperative imaging studies revealed no intracranial complications and confirmed that the drainage pathway remained patent.ConclusionIn the differential diagnosis of lesions in the medial portion of the petrous apex, a mucocele should be considered. In appropriately selected cases, endoscopic endonasal marsupialization can be an effective option. To maintain postoperative patency of the drainage pathway, an implant containing mometasone furoate may also be used.

title: Rare Migrated Fishbone Foreign Body in the Nasopharynx.
abstract: Although impaction of the pharyngoesophageal fishbone represents a common otolaryngological emergency, migration of an ingested fish bone into the nasopharynx is an extremely rare clinical occurrence. We present a 57-year-old woman who developed acute odynophagia one hour after fish ingestion, accompanied by a single choking episode, in the absence of nausea or vomiting. The oropharyngeal examination at the bedside failed to identify any foreign body. Given the patient's refusal to computed tomography (CT), she was discharged for outpatient surveillance. Twenty-four hours later, she returned with persistent refractory pharyngeal pain. Repeated pharyngeal endoscopy revealed neither foreign material nor mucosal injury. Multiplanar coronal CT reconstruction identified a 2.63 cm linear hyperattenuating bone fragment within the nasopharyngeal cavity. After topical nasal decongestion, flexible fiberoptic nasopharyngoscopy confirmed a partially embedded migrated fish bone, which was successfully retrieved endoscopically using alligator grasping forceps. Odynophagia resolved immediately after extraction and the patient remained asymptomatic throughout the 2 week follow-up. For patients with persistent pharyngeal pain and high clinical suspicion of retained foreign bodies despite negative physical examination and endoscopic findings, CT should be considered the first-line cross-sectional modality to prevent missed.diagnoses and life-threatening cervicofacial septic complications.

Twenty-four hours later, she returned with persistent refractory pharyngeal pain. Repeated pharyngeal endoscopy revealed neither foreign material nor mucosal injury. Multiplanar coronal CT reconstruction identified a 2.63 cm linear hyperattenuating bone fragment within the nasopharyngeal cavity. After topical nasal decongestion, flexible fiberoptic nasopharyngoscopy confirmed a partially embedded migrated fish bone, which was successfully retrieved endoscopically using alligator grasping forceps. Odynophagia resolved immediately after extraction and the patient remained asymptomatic throughout the 2 week follow-up. For patients with persistent pharyngeal pain and high clinical suspicion of retained foreign bodies despite negative physical examination and endoscopic findings, CT should be considered the first-line cross-sectional modality to prevent missed.diagnoses and life-threatening cervicofacial septic complications.

title: Recognizing Odontogenic Maxillary Sinusitis in the ENT Clinic: Four CT Findings That Should Prompt Dental Evaluation.
abstract: Objective: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the proportion of maxillary sinuses with radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution among patients with imaging-confirmed acute or chronic maxillary sinusitis presenting to a single academic ENT clinic over one year. Sixty-five CT scans (84 sinuses) underwent multidisciplinary review for prespecified radiographic features. By highlighting imaging findings indicative of dental origin this study aims to improve recognition of possible odontogenic disease and appropriate multidisciplinary evaluation. Methods: Sixty-five patients were evaluated. Inclusion criteria required a visit diagnosis of chronic maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J32.0) or acute maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J01.00, J01.01), and a sinus CT within the preceding year. Each scan underwent multidisciplinary review by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist, an otolaryngologist, an otolaryngology resident, and a medical student. Scans were evaluated for maxillary sinus floor mucosal thickening and radiographic features suggestive of an odontogenic contribution, including periapical pathology, oroantral communication, large dental restorations, and widened periodontal ligament (PDL) space. Dental referral recommendations were based on multidisciplinary consensus from CT findings alone. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics. Results: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution were identified in 50/84 (59.52%) affected maxillary sinuses from 40 patients. Among these 50 sinuses, 17 (34%) showed widened PDL space, 15 (30%) showed oroantral communication, 28 (56%) showed periapical pathology, and 9 (18%) showed large dental restorations. There was consensus among the multidisciplinary team that in retrospect, among the 40 patients with OS, 38 required dental referrals. Conclusion: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution indicated a higher single-center cohort prevalence than expected based on population-level prevalence reports. The findings support deliberate review of the maxillary dentition on sinus CT, with this study outlining the key imaging features for odontogenic sinusitis.

title: MTL-LymphNet: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Framework for Simultaneous Lymph Node Segmentation and Metastasis Classification in Thyroid Cancer Ultrasound.
abstract: Ultrasound assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma is crucial but suffers from inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning solutions typically use separate single-task pipelines, resulting in parameter redundancy. We propose MTL-LymphNet, a lightweight, backbone-agnostic multi-task learning framework that simultaneously segments lymph nodes and classifies metastasis within a single forward pass, evaluated across 3 backbones and 4 loss weighting strategies. On 338 images from 2 independent clinical centers, MTL-LymphNet achieved an internal cross-validation Dice coefficient of 0.891 ± 0.022 and AUC of 0.948 ± 0.027. Bidirectional external validation revealed substantial domain shift, with cross-center Dice of 0.865 and 0.779, and AUC of 0.733 and 0.830. The multi-task configuration offered a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off (∆Dice = Δ, -0.014, P < .0001) for 40% fewer parameters than separate models. No backbone or weighting strategy consistently dominated, and calibration degraded substantially under domain shift (ECE: 0.049 internally vs 0.178-0.304 externally), requiring center-specific recalibration before clinical use. To our knowledge, this is the first MTL framework for cervical lymph node analysis with bidirectional multi-center validation and systematic ablation. With a compact size of 22.6 to 29.1 MB and CPU inference of 81 to 131 ms, MTL-LymphNet demonstrates technical feasibility as a CAD tool warranting prospective validation.

title: Rapid noncontrast MRI screening for iliac and left renal vein compression: A practical bSSFP technique.
abstract: ObjectivesTo describe a rapid, widely available, noncontrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for first-line morphologic assessment of suspected iliac and left renal vein compression in patients with symptoms potentially related to pelvic venous disorders.MethodsWe use a two-stack axial two-dimensional balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) acquisition extending from the renal hila through the iliac bifurcation. The sequence is available on major MRI platforms as TrueFISP (Siemens), FIESTA (GE), or bTFE (Philips). Typical 1.5-T parameters are TR/TE 3.0-3.8/1.5-1.9 ms, flip angle 60-80°, 5-mm slice thickness, and 1.3-1.6-mm in-plane resolution. Localized shimming is performed for each stack.ResultsThe abbreviated examination requires approximately 10 minutes of scanner time, including planning and breath-hold acquisitions. It depicts the site and degree of iliac or left renal vein compression and demonstrates collateral pathways that may support physiologic relevance. Morphologic abnormalities are interpreted in the clinical context and are not considered diagnostic of a symptomatic syndrome in isolation.ConclusionsA short bSSFP protocol can provide a practical, radiation-free gateway examination when comprehensive MR venography is unavailable or undesirable. It may facilitate appropriate referral and procedural planning, while invasive assessment, including intravascular ultrasound when stenting is contemplated, remains necessary in selected patients.

title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
abstract: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) ( p < 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m 2 , p < 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT ( p = 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.

title: LipoVena AI framework: A physician-centered artificial intelligence-assisted approach for longitudinal assessment in lipedema and chronic venous disorders.
abstract: BackgroundChronic venous disorders and lipedema are complex and frequently underdiagnosed conditions characterized by heterogeneous clinical presentations, progressive tissue remodeling, and substantial variability in treatment response assessment. Despite advances in minimally invasive vascular interventions, longitudinal evaluation in routine clinical practice continues to rely heavily on subjective interpretation, non-standardized comparative imaging, and physician-dependent assessment pathways. The integration of multimodal vascular data into structured longitudinal clinical workflows remains limited.ObjectiveThis study introduces the LipoVena AI Framework, a physician-centered conceptual artificial intelligence-assisted clinical support architecture designed to facilitate multimodal integration, longitudinal treatment-response evaluation, and personalized monitoring in lipedema and chronic venous disease management.MethodsA retrospective observational clinical dataset consisting of 32 patients with chronic venous insufficiency, lipedema, reticular veins, spider veins, and mixed venous-lymphatic phenotypes was reviewed. Standardized standing-position photography, duplex ultrasound imaging, procedural documentation, and longitudinal 1-month follow-up assessments were integrated within a conceptual AI-assisted workflow. Representative patients underwent multimodal minimally invasive treatment strategies including endovenous laser therapy (EVLT), CLACS-guided sclerotherapy, radiofrequency-based tissue remodeling, and compression therapy. The proposed framework conceptually integrates multimodal imaging analysis, vascular mapping, comparative longitudinal assessment, and physician-supervised AI-assisted interpretation.ResultsRepresentative 1-month follow-up observations demonstrated visible improvements in contour harmonization, superficial venous prominence, tissue irregularity, skin texture uniformity, and vascular burden across multiple venous and lipedema phenotypes. Comparative multimodal analysis integrating clinical photography and duplex ultrasound findings enabled structured longitudinal assessment of therapeutic response patterns. Upper-extremity lipedema cases additionally demonstrated measurable contour and tissue-texture improvement following multimodal treatment strategies. The proposed framework illustrated the potential role of AI-assisted longitudinal comparison and multimodal integration in supporting objective treatment-response evaluation within physician-centered vascular care workflows.ConclusionThe LipoVena AI Framework presents a conceptual translational model for future AI-assisted vascular and lipedema medicine by integrating standardized clinical imaging, duplex ultrasound evaluation, multimodal treatment documentation, and longitudinal follow-up analysis within a physician-centered ecosystem. Although prospective multicenter validation and quantitative AI modeling remain necessary, the present framework highlights the potential of explainable and physician-supervised artificial intelligence systems to support personalized, data-driven, and longitudinally optimized vascular care.

title: EXPRESS: Longitudinal Quantitative MRI of Blood-Brain Barrier Leakage in Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion Rat model.
abstract: Objective-Methods:Chronic cerebral-hypoperfusion is a key contributor to vascular cognitive impairment, with blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction proposed as an early driver of white matter injury. The temporal-evolution and regional-heterogeneity of BBB-leakage remain poorly characterized in vivo. We longitudinally assessed BBB permeability in Sprague-Dawley rats subjected to bilateral-common carotid artery occlusion (2VO) versus sham controls using contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI 9.4T over 12-weeks. Gadolinium-leakage maps were generated and analyzed in predefined regions (cortex, hippocampus, striatum, corpus callosum). Exploratory histological observations included GFAP immunostaining, and circulating biochemical biomarkers (sTWEAK, MMP-9, GOT, cytokines) were quantified.Results:Localized BBB disruption was observed at weeks 3, 6 post-2VO and progressed heterogeneously, with pronounced leakage strictly targeted toward corpus callosum, hippocampus and striatum. Despite descriptive trends showing increased astroglial activation, systemic biochemical biomarkers did not correlate with imaging-derived central BBB-leakage. Volumetric analysis revealed subtle but significant brain atrophy (18% whole-brain reduction) preceding overt T2-signal abnormalities. In the 2VO model studied, BBB dysfunction in chronic-hypoperfusion appears to be a dynamic, region-specific process.Conclusion:Longitudinal contrast-enhanced MRI detected changes that were not mirrored by the circulating biomarkers studied, suggesting its potential utility as a surrogate endpoint in preclinical studies, which should be confirmed in larger cohorts and complementary models.

title: EXPRESS: Diagnostic and prognostic value of on-site CT-derived fractional flow reserve in intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
abstract: Background The role of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) in cerebrovascular disease remains undefined. This study validated the diagnostic and prognostic value of an on-site CT-FFR in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS) patients. Methods This retrospective study enrolled sICAS patients with 30 - 99% stenosis confirmed by CTA, divided into two substudies. The diagnostic performance study included 259 patients undergoing CTA and CT perfusion (CTP) or four-dimensional CTA (CTP as reference standard). In prognosis study, 452 patients with at least 1-year follow-up were included. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was used to measure CT-FFR. Diagnostic performance was assessed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and predictive value by Cox regression analysis. Results The diagnostic performance of CT-FFR was significantly higher than diameter stenosis (DS) on both per-patient (P = 0.009) and per-lesion (P = 0.004) basis. And the cut-off value of CT-FFR diagnosing cerebral hypoperfusion was 0.80. 15.0% (68 / 452) patients experienced recurrent ischemic events during the median 24 (17-33) months follow-up. CT-FFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond traditional cardiovascular risks plus DS (AUC = 0.797 vs 0.716, P < 0.001). Conclusion This on-site CT-FFR can serve as a valuable tool for diagnosis and risk stratification in sICAS patients.

title: EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

title: Cardiac diagnostic modalities in polycythemia vera: A narrative review.
abstract: Polycythemia vera is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm in which erythrocytosis, Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal blood-cell activation converge to increase cardiovascular risk. This narrative review examines how electrocardiography, echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and right-heart catheterization contribute to recognition and characterization of cardiac involvement in polycythemia vera. Reported abnormalities include QT and P-wave changes, atrial arrhythmias, acute coronary syndromes, subclinical biventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, intracardiac thrombosis, and hypertrophic remodeling. Large observational datasets in myeloproliferative neoplasms also exhibit clinically important burdens of myocardial infarction, heart-failure hospitalization, bleeding, and echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension, although polycythemia vera-specific estimates remain limited. Baseline cardiovascular testing is increasingly relevant before novel therapies and trial enrollment; however, an abnormal test should prompt confirmation, reversible-cause assessment, and protocol-specific review rather than be treated as a universal contraindication. Hematocrit control and low-dose aspirin reduce thrombotic events, while evidence that cytoreductive therapy reverses electrocardiography or imaging abnormalities remains sparse. A symptom- and risk-directed diagnostic approach, integrated with hematology and cardiology assessment, is therefore more defensible than routine universal cardiac screening.
