title: Evaluation of Management Pathways for Pseudophakic Cystoid Macular Edema in a Large United States Cohort.
abstract: Purpose To identify the common management pathways in the treatment of pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME). Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2005 to 2024 using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with pseudophakic CME were included in the study, and patients with retinal comorbidities were excluded. Treatments initiated after the diagnosis of pseudophakic CME, including topical corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), periocular and intravitreal (IVT) corticosteroids, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections, suprachoroidal corticosteroids, and pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), were tracked, and treatment sequences and imaging use over time were analyzed. Results A total of 23 035 patients met the inclusion criteria, with a mean age of 72 years; 54% were women, and 68% identified as White. The incidence of pseudophakic CME increased from 2.45% in 2005 to 17.6% in 2024. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) use increased over time, becoming the most common imaging modality (used in 90% of cases), while 20% of patients underwent no imaging. No treatment was documented in 40% of patients. Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon. Conclusions Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

Purpose

To identify the common management pathways in the treatment of pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME).

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2005 to 2024 using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with pseudophakic CME were included in the study, and patients with retinal comorbidities were excluded. Treatments initiated after the diagnosis of pseudophakic CME, including topical corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), periocular and intravitreal (IVT) corticosteroids, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections, suprachoroidal corticosteroids, and pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), were tracked, and treatment sequences and imaging use over time were analyzed.

Results

A total of 23 035 patients met the inclusion criteria, with a mean age of 72 years; 54% were women, and 68% identified as White. The incidence of pseudophakic CME increased from 2.45% in 2005 to 17.6% in 2024. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) use increased over time, becoming the most common imaging modality (used in 90% of cases), while 20% of patients underwent no imaging. No treatment was documented in 40% of patients. Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon.

Conclusions

Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

title: Germ line landscape stratification defines distinct molecular and prognostic groups in therapy-related myeloid neoplasms.
abstract: Abstract Exposure to chemotherapy (CT) and/or radiotherapy increases the risk of therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MN), a heterogeneous group of disorders currently classified by treatment history rather than molecular features. Although germ line predisposition has been suggested in ∼20% of patients, its prevalence and clinical impact remain insufficiently defined. To address this, we analyzed 100 patients with t-MN by integrating clinical characteristics, prior treatment regimens, and genomic profiling. Somatic and germ line variants were identified using targeted next-generation sequencing (n = 33) or whole-exome sequencing (n = 67). Somatic abnormalities, including cytogenetic and/or molecular alterations, were detected in 89.8% of patients. Germ line variants were identified in 32.3% of patients, including mutations in cancer predisposition genes (19.8%) and myeloid disease-related genes (14.6%). Patient stratification by germ line landscape and gene category defined 2 prognostic scenarios and 3 subgroups with distinct clinical outcomes. Patients harboring germ line cancer predisposition variants were enriched for TP53 mutations and complex karyotypes and had an adverse prognosis. In contrast, patients with germ line myeloid-related variants and those without detectable germ line variants exhibited recurrent mutations in TET2, DNMT3A, SF3B1, SRSF2, RUNX1, and ASXL1, were associated with normal karyotypes, and had favorable outcomes. These findings underscore the importance of the germ line landscape in t-MN pathogenesis and support its incorporation into disease classification and risk stratification. Notably, CT exposure was associated with complex karyotypes and poor prognosis in patients with germ line cancer predisposition variants, highlighting a subgroup that may benefit from targeted surveillance and preventive strategies.

title: Prognosis and treatment-related toxicities in Down syndrome acute lymphoblastic leukemia in JCCG ALL-B12.
abstract: Children with Down syndrome (DS) have an increased risk of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Although recent reports describe some improvement, survival in DS-ALL remains inferior to that of non-DS-ALL. This study evaluated the prognosis, relapse patterns, and treatment-related toxicities of DS-ALL in the Japan Children's Cancer Group ALL-B12 trial, a nationwide prospective study using risk-adapted therapy. A total of 1,804 patients, including 44 DS-ALL, were analyzed. Risk classification used standardized criteria. The 5-year event-free survival and overall survival in DS-ALL were 70.5% and 81.8%, respectively, lower than 85.6% and 94.6% in non-DS-ALL (P < 0.001). Survival differences were most pronounced in standard-risk patients. DS-ALL showed fewer favorable genetics and relapse patterns dominated by isolated bone marrow events, with no CNS relapse. CRLF2 rearrangement was assessable in 43 of 44 DS-ALL cases; 15 of 43 (34.9%) were positive. In an exploratory analysis excluding canonical favorable or unfavorable subtypes (n = 36), the 5-year EFS in DS-ALL with and without CRLF2 rearrangement were 57.1% and 81.8%, respectively (P = 0.300), and the corresponding 5-year OS were 78.6% and 86.4%, respectively (P = 0.331). Treatment-related toxicities were more frequent in DS-ALL, including mucositis (27.3% vs. 7.1%), hyperglycemia (25.0% vs. 6.9%), and pulmonary infections (20.5% vs. 7.4%). title: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis in a monogenic mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome.
abstract: Background Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) is a rare, most often idiopathic fibrotic lung disease with poor prognosis, mainly affecting adults. Biallelic pathogenic variants in the deoxyguanosine kinase gene ( DGUOK ) cause a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion syndrome, predominantly affecting infants with severe hepatic and neurological disease. Neither detailed pulmonary manifestations nor a pulmonary-dominant phenotype has been reported. Methods We describe nine patients with PPFE and DGUOK -associated mitochondriopathy. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were systematically collected from all patients. Functional studies, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNAseq), immunofluorescence staining, transmission electron microscopy, respiratory chain enzyme activity assays and mtDNA recovery experiment were conducted on patient-derived fibroblasts, muscle or lung tissues. mtDNA content quantification was performed on whole genome sequencing data. Results All patients (ages 5-36 years) carried biallelic pathogenic DGUOK variants, including an unreported intronic alteration in seven. All presented with progressive dyspnea, weight loss and some with pneumothoraces. Chest computed tomography and lung biopsies demonstrated features of PPFE. snRNAseq of lung tissue from four pediatric patients identified Aberrant Basaloid cells at the fibrotic edge, together with a transcriptional signature of nuclear DNA damage response. Ultrastructural analysis confirmed mitochondrial abnormalities in alveolar type 2 and Aberrant Basaloid cells. Conclusion This study provides evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction can contribute to early-onset PPFE independent of age, with a DNA damage response signature in aberrant epithelial cell populations previously described only in adult fibrotic lung disease. DGUOK deficiency and other hereditary mitochondrial disorders should be considered in children and young adults presenting with PPFE of unknown origin.

title: Interventions to increase participation in lung cancer screening programmes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT). Methods Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion. Results Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Educational/informational interventions (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.19) as well as SDM alone (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.57-2.32) did not improve LDCT uptake, despite the second improving decisional outcomes in both intervention and control groups. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare. Conclusions Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

title: Geriatric respiratory medicine 2026: from artificial intelligence to personalised management of the multimorbid patient.
abstract: The profound demographic shift toward an ageing population has decisively moved the burden of chronic and acute lung diseases towards older adults, necessitating a transition from organ-centred models to integrated, multidimensional care. This review outlines a pragmatic framework for managing the complex interplay of immunosenescence, frailty and multimorbidity. In acute care, "pneumonia-associated sarcopenia" is identified as a critical driver of recurrent infections and functional decline, requiring a shift towards aspiration prevention and the aid of diagnostic tools such as lung ultrasound. The selection of noninvasive respiratory support, including high-flow nasal cannulas and noninvasive ventilation, must balance physiological efficacy with the risks of delirium and patient self-inflicted lung injury. Preventive strategies have evolved with the introduction of 20-valent pneumococcal and respiratory syncytial virus vaccines, alongside proactive screening for ɑ1-antitrypsin deficiency to enable precision interventions. Chronic disease management emphasises a "device-centric" inhalation therapy approach, tailoring delivery systems to impaired peak inspiratory flows and cognitive status rather than to pharmacology alone. The advent of biological therapies, particularly the use of dupilumab and mepolizumab in eosinophilic COPD, offers a transformative "steroid-sparing" effect, aiming for clinical stability and preserved independence. Finally, the integration of artificial intelligence as "augmented intelligence" and the "4Ms" multidisciplinary model (mentation, medication, mobility, morbidities) provide the necessary tools to navigate clinical complexity. This holistic strategy ensures that technological innovation remains anchored in patient-centred goals.

title: Development of <sup>99m</sup>Tc-cefadroxil loaded chitosan nanoparticles as a novel radiotracer for detection of septic and aseptic foci.
abstract: Early detection of inflammation is critical for preventing disease progression, and nuclear medicine plays a pivotal role in this context. Imaging modalities such as single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) enable the early identification of functional abnormalities through the use of targeted radiotracers that specifically localize inflammatory processes. In this regard, antibiotic-loaded nanoparticles have emerged as a promising platform for inflammation imaging, integrating diagnostic capabilities with potential therapeutic functionality. Among these systems, chitosan-based nanocarriers (CS-NPs), a nano-polymeric pharmaceutical excipient, were employed for the encapsulation of the antibiotic cefadroxil (CDX). The formulation was prepared via a simple ionic gelation (cross-linking) technique. The physicochemical properties of the resulting nanoparticles were characterized using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), zeta potential analysis, and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Drug encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were subsequently quantified by UV-visible spectrophotometry. For imaging applications, CDX-loaded CS-NPs (400 µg) were radiolabeled with technetium-99m in the presence of stannous chloride (50 µg) as a reducing agent, yielding a complex with a radiochemical efficiency of 94 ± 1.3%. The resulting 99mTc-CDX-CS-NPs demonstrated excellent in vitro stability in fresh serum for up to 6 hours, which is suitable for diagnostic imaging applications. In vivo biodistribution studies in murine models of both septic and aseptic inflammation revealed significant tracer accumulation at infected and inflamed sites, with high target-to-non-target (T/NT) ratios of 8.55 and 6.02 after 2 hours post-injection, respectively. These findings suggest the developed radiotracer's ability to effectually localize septic and aseptic foci, irrespective of their underlying etiology.

title: Impact of reduced scan extent on tumor detection in <sup>68</sup>Ga-PSMA PET/CT for biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer.
abstract: Background PSMA PET/CT plays an important role in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BCR-PCa). In general, PET/CT is performed as a limited or true whole-body examination. The majority of PET/CT scanners operate by measuring several bed positions or continuous motion with a limited axial field of view (FOV). Shortening the scan area thus results in a time saving, with unknown information loss regarding the detection of tumor manifestations. Methodology This retrospective single-center study included 200 patients with BCR-PCa after initial curative therapy who underwent a 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT scan from vertex to toe (true whole-body). Using retrospective subdivision into hypothetical partial body measurement protocols, the undetected tumor manifestations were examined. Classic PET/CT protocols were used: vertex to mid-thigh, skull base to mid-thigh, as well as CT-equivalent examination areas: chest/abdomen/pelvis (CAP), abdomen/pelvis (AP) and pelvis. Results Of 200 patients with a median PSA of 1.1 ng/mL, 128 (64%) showed at least one structural correlate of BCR-PCa in the true whole-body scan. The overall detection rate did not change for limited classic PET-protocols, or CAP measurements. CAP scans would not have detected all tumor manifestations in 16 patients (8%) and not all tumor-affected organ systems in six patients (3%), AP scans in 41 patients (21%) and 18 patients (9%), pelvic scans in 61 patients (31%) and 37 patients (19%), respectively. PSA may contribute to the prospective restriction of the scan area. Patients with PSA ≤ 0.75 ng/mL showed no diagnostic gain from whole-body imaging. This means that in 45% of patients in our cohort, a limitation to CAP scan would have been possible without losing information. Conclusions For a resource-saving use of routine PSMA-PET/CT, a scan from the vertex to the mid-thigh seems sufficient for detecting relevant metastases. For patients with low PSA levels, a more focused protocol that includes only the CAP region can be considered.

title: Non-Ischemic Cerebral Enhancing (NICE) lesions after flow diversion for intracranial aneurysms: a systematic review with case-level synthesis.
abstract: Background Non-ischemic cerebral enhancing (NICE) lesions are rare delayed inflammatory brain lesions reported after flow-diverter (FD) treatment of intracranial aneurysms. We systematically reviewed their reported incidence, clinical and imaging characteristics, diagnostic findings, management, and outcomes. Methods We performed a PROSPERO-registered systematic review. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched for reports of delayed NICE lesions after FD treatment of intracranial aneurysms that were not better explained by infarction or alternative causes. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Findings were synthesized narratively because heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Results Twenty-two studies met inclusion criteria; seven reported incidence data. One multicenter survey provided the only FD-specific denominator (12 NICE cases among 1201 FD-treated aneurysms; 1.0%), but the true incidence remains uncertain. Other estimates, using all aneurysm endovascular procedures as denominators, ranged from 0.05% to 1.3%. Overall, 40 unique FD-associated NICE patients were identified. Among cases with available individual data, median age was 54 years; all patients with reported sex were women, and all aneurysms with reported location involved the anterior circulation. NICE lesions appeared after a median of 73 days, most often with headache, focal deficits, or seizures, and as multifocal, predominantly ipsilateral enhancing lesions with edema on MRI. Brain biopsy was performed in six patients and identified hydrophilic polymer or other foreign material in four; in one additional case, device-coating detachment was observed directly. Both coated and uncoated FDs were represented, although the source component was usually undetermined. Systemic corticosteroids were administered in 22/24 cases with treatment data. Radiologic improvement or resolution occurred in 12/25, recurrent or fluctuating activity in 11/25, and 19/23 patients with reported functional outcomes were asymptomatic or independent at last follow-up. Conclusions Reported NICE lesions after flow diversion appear uncommon, but the true incidence remains uncertain. The available evidence supports a foreign-body inflammatory mechanism potentially related to hydrophilic coatings or other materials within the endovascular construct, without establishing a single culprit device. Corticosteroid-associated improvement is common, but relapsing or fluctuating courses require prolonged clinical and imaging follow-up. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD420251186127.

title: Prediction of death by neurologic criteria in patients with non-traumatic acute brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Robust predictors of death by neurologic criteria (DNC) after non-traumatic acute brain injury remain insufficiently defined. We therefore aimed to systematically synthesize the available evidence on prediction of DNC in non-traumatic brain injury. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched to August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, case series and registry data. Studies were included in the quantitative synthesis when sufficient comparable data for the same prognostic factor were available from at least two studies. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Results The database search identified 2,091 records. Eighteen studies comprising reported study cohorts of 9,070 participants were included. Quantitative synthesis included four studies (n=1,738), comprising two post-cardiac arrest and two stroke cohorts. In stroke populations, CT markers of severe intracranial mass effect were associated with a more than threefold increased odds of DNC (pooled OR 3.14, 95%CI 1.98-4.96; p<0.0001; I2=0%), while in post-cardiac arrest cohorts lower gray-white matter ratio values were associated with progression to DNC (pooled mean difference -0.15, 95%CI -0.22 to -0.07; p<0.001; I2=72%). Conclusions Evidence on predictors of DNC after non-traumatic acute brain injury remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous, with only a small number of studies providing robust analyses. Across these studies, CT-based markers - particularly indicators of diffuse cerebral edema or intracranial mass effect - show the most reproducible associations with progression to DNC.

title: Late enhancement and washout maps for distinguishing tumor progression from radiation necrosis in malignant brain tumors: an exploratory study.
abstract: Background Distinguishing between tumor progression and radiation necrosis during brain tumor follow-up is challenging. Advanced MR imaging techniques, such as perfusion, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and spectroscopy, can help differentiate between these conditions. In our clinic, we established a novel technique, the rapid washout and late-enhancement map. This study investigated the value of this map in distinguishing true progression from radiation necrosis. Methods Patients with a histologically confirmed initial diagnosis of glioblastoma, high-grade astrocytoma, primary central nervous system lymphoma, or brain metastasis who were undergoing radiochemotherapy and participated in our MRI protocol, including MR perfusion and rapid washout imaging, between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025, were included in the study. We volumetrically measured late enhancement and washout in brain tumors at all follow-up examinations and analyzed the resulting volumes. Additionally, we evaluated diffusion-weighted imaging and MR perfusion images. Results A total of 33 patients (25 with glioblastoma, two with astrocytoma grade 4, two with astrocytoma grade 3, one with CNS lymphoma, and three with brain metastasis) were included. Diagnostic confirmation was obtained by histopathological assessment in 20 patients, MRI follow-up in 13 patients, with additional fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography in two. Among these patients, 23 were diagnosed with tumor recurrence, four with mixed pathology comprising "radiation necrosis with scattered active tumor cells", and six with radiation necrosis. The mean washout ratio (± standard deviation) was 31 ± 18 % for progressive disease, 35 ± 20 % for mixed pathology, and 10 ± 7 % for radiation necrosis, respectively. Conclusions The washout ratio can enhance the differentiation between recurrent tumor growth and radiation necrosis during post-treatment monitoring of malignant brain tumors. As MR perfusion can yield inconclusive results in this setting, the proposed method offers complementary information that supports initial diagnostic decision making. Diagnostic discrimination may be strengthened by combining the relative cerebral blood volume with washout ratio analysis, rather than relying on a single imaging marker.

title: Intravitreal methotrexate as a prophylactic strategy for proliferative vitreoretinopathy in high-risk retinal detachment.
abstract: Background Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) remains the major cause of surgical failure in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD). This study evaluates the anatomical and functional outcomes, as well as the safety, of a standardized intraoperative intravitreal methotrexate infusion protocol during pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in eyes with early stage PVR (grade B) or with advanced PVR (grade C). Methods A retrospective case series was conducted on 60 consecutive eyes of 59 patients with RRD and PVR grade B (n = 29) or grade C (n = 31) undergoing PPV with adjunct intraoperative methotrexate between November 2024 and February 2026 at a German tertiary center. Methotrexate 40 mg was administered via a 500 mL balanced salt solution infusion. Functional and structural testing included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure, multifocal electroretinogram, perimetry, and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography. The primary outcome measure was single-surgery anatomical success (SSAS) at 12 weeks after primary surgery or after silicone oil removal. Secondary outcomes included BCVA changes and complication rates. Results SSAS was achieved in 81.7% of all eyes, with a significantly higher success rate in eyes with PVR grade B compared to PVR grade C (93.1% versus 71.0%; p = 0.043). At 12 weeks, BCVA improved significantly in macula-off cases (p < 0.001) and remained stable in macula-on cases. In an exploratory subset of 17 patients postoperative multifocal electroretinogram and perimetry demonstrated preserved central retinal function. No ocular or systemic adverse events related to methotrexate occurred. Conclusions The standardized intraoperative intravitreal methotrexate infusion protocol was safe, feasible, and associated with high single-surgery reattachment rates, particularly in PVR grade B eyes. Anatomical outcomes in PVR grade C eyes were comparable to other complex PVR cohorts, without any drug-related local or systemic toxicity. Trial registration Not applicable (retrospective observational study).

title: Who participates in LDCT screening for the early detection of lung cancer after long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust? Results of the analysis of administrative and medical routine data from the German Social Accident Insurance.
abstract: Background Lung cancer is one of the most common cancers in Germany and is predominantly detected at an advanced stage. To ensure early detection, the German Social Accident Insurance (DGUV) offers lung cancer screening including a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) for individuals with long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust and a smoking history of at least 30 pack years. However, evidence remains scarce about what encourages this group of people to participate in LDCT screening after medical consultation. Methods A secondary data analysis using routinely collected medical and administrative data between 2014 and 2024 was conducted in a cross-sectional design. This study aimed to investigate factors that could be used to predict the uptake of LDCT screening following a medical consultation. Exploratory logistic regression analysis was used to identify and assess possible predictors. Results The sample included n = 14,491 individuals (97% male; average age 67 years; average asbestos dust exposure 21 years; average cigarette consumption 43 pack years). 74% of individuals underwent LDCT screening after medical consultation. 13 predictors were included in the regression model. The model demonstrated a low level of variance explanation (Nagelkerkes R 2 = 0.026). Younger individuals (OR: 0.96, p < 0.001), individuals with prolonged exposure to asbestos dust (OR: 1.01, p = 0.011) and with a history of pneumonia (OR: 1.16, p = 0.011) were more likely to undergo LDCT screening. Conclusion The predictors showed only a low explanatory power. Further research should include non-participants and expand the exploratory model to include theoretically grounded predictors.

title: Routine versus postoperative CRP/CT guided selective diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a comparative randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Background Diverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak. This trial evaluated whether a postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and computed tomography (CT) guided selective ileostomy strategy could reduce the rate of ileostomy formation compared with routine diversion. Methods In this RCT, 200 patients with stage II or III middle or lower third rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic LAR were randomized 1:1 to a CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy group (n = 100) or a routine diverting ileostomy group (n = 100). In the CRP/CT group, serum CRP was measured daily from postoperative day 1; a threshold of 114 mg/L on day 3 or a rise greater than 15 mg/L per day triggered confirmatory contrast-enhanced CT, with ileostomy formed only if findings were suspicious for leak. The primary outcome was the stoma-free status throughout the 12-month follow-up. Results Baseline demographic and tumor characteristics were similar between groups (all p > 0.05). Ileostomy formation was markedly lower in the CRP/CT group than the routine group (22.0% vs. 100.0%, p < 0.001). Anastomotic leak rates did not differ (0% vs. 1.0%, p = 1.000), nor did overall complication rates (31.0% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.879). Operative time (148.4 ± 14.0 vs. 166.6 ± 13.1 min, p < 0.001) and intraoperative blood loss (168.9 ± 28.2 vs. 197.3 ± 39.7 mL, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the CRP/CT group. Stoma-related complications were far less frequent with the selective strategy (3.0% vs. 30.0%, p < 0.001). The CRP/CT group reported significantly better global health status, physical functioning, and emotional functioning scores (all p < 0.001). Conclusion A postoperative CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy strategy reduces the need for diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer while improving operative outcomes and quality of life; however, confirmed leakage was infrequent in both groups. This approach may serve as an alternative to routine diversion in appropriately monitored surgical units. Trial registration This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07722533) on July 17, 2026.

title: Right upper lobectomy via selective right upper lobe isolation using a left-sided double-lumen tube placed in the right bronchus intermedius: a case report.
abstract: Background One-lung ventilation (OLV) using a left-sided double-lumen tube (DLT) in the left main bronchus is standard for right thoracic surgery. When the contralateral left lung is severely compromised, this approach forces OLV to rely on the dysfunctional lung and risks critical hypoxemia. Case presentation An 84-year-old woman with a left diaphragmatic hernia causing approximately 70% compression and atelectasis of the left lung was scheduled for right upper lobectomy. Preoperative assessment indicated that standard DLT placement would necessitate complete right lung collapse, placing the patient at risk of life-threatening hypoxemia. A 32-Fr left-sided DLT was intentionally inserted into the right bronchus intermedius under fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FOB). The bronchial cuff was positioned at the orifice of the right upper lobe (RUL) bronchus to achieve selective occlusion. Ventilation was delivered through the tracheal lumen to the left lung and through the bronchial lumen to the right middle and lower lobes. The RUL collapsed completely. Intraoperative oxygenation remained stable, with SpO 2 greater than 95%. The patient underwent an uneventful thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy, was extubated immediately after surgery, and was discharged on postoperative day 6. Conclusions Intentional placement of a left-sided DLT into the right bronchus intermedius is a feasible strategy for selective RUL isolation when standard OLV is contraindicated due to severe contralateral lung compromise. Preoperative computed tomography (CT)-based airway assessment and fiberoptic bronchoscopic guidance are recommended for safe implementation.

title: Effect of injectable platelet rich fibrin augmented with vitamin c compared to injectable platelet rich fibrin alone on healing of necrotic mature single rooted teeth with chronic periapical periodontitis following regenerative endodontic therapy (a randomized controlled trial).
abstract: Objectives To assess the healing potential, postoperative pain and clinical normalcy associated with injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C in regenerative endodontic procedure using cone-beam computed tomography and two-dimensional radiograph. Methods Twenty-eight healthy patients with mature permanent single-rooted teeth diagnosed with pulp necrosis and chronic apical periodontitis were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 14). Regenerative endodontic treatment was performed using injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C (intervention group) and injectable platelet-rich fibrin alone (control group). Periapical healing was assessed using CBCT and periapical radiographs over 12 months. Postoperative pain and clinical normalcy were also evaluated. Results Both groups showed significant lesion reduction at 12 months (P = 0.001), with no significant between-group differences in postoperative lesion size (P = 0.981) or reduction magnitude (P = 0.497). CBCT-PAI scores improved in both groups without significant intergroup differences at baseline or follow-up. Two-dimensional radiographs showed a baseline difference (P = 0.007) but no postoperative differences; both groups demonstrated significant longitudinal reduction (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain scores were comparable between groups at all time points (P > 0.05), with a significant temporal decrease observed only in the intervention group (P = 0.001). All teeth remained asymptomatic during follow-up. Conclusions Both i-PRF combined with vitamin C and i-PRF alone appear to be effective regenerative scaffolds, demonstrating comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes in regenerative endodontic procedures. Clinical trial registration The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT05585359), registered on 14 October 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05585359 .

title: CT-based 3D morphometric reference data on osseous TMJ subunits in a European cohort: relevance for patient-specific implant research.
abstract: Background Patient-specific alloplastic prostheses are increasingly used for reconstruction of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). However, the extent to which articulating implant components should reflect native osseous TMJ morphology remains unresolved. This study used CT-derived three-dimensional (3D) virtual-digital surface models to analyze osseous TMJ subunits in humans and provide morphometric reference data for future patient-specific TMJ implant research. Methods In this retrospective exploratory study, 97 computed tomography (CT) scans from Hannover Medical School were analyzed. High-quality 3D virtual-digital models of the articulating TMJ subunits, including the mandibular condyle and glenoid fossa, were generated and used to measure relevant TMJ parameters. Parameters were compared according to sex and age, and correlation analyses were performed. Results Morphometric variability was observed among the osseous TMJ subunits. Men showed larger medial-lateral diameters of the mandibular condyle, greater articular tubercle height, and larger zygomatic arch root dimensions. Women showed a larger anterior-posterior diameter of the glenoid fossa. Middle-aged participants showed a larger anterior-posterior diameter of the mandibular condyle and larger sagittal dimensions of the zygomatic arch root compared with young-aged participants. Correlation analysis revealed associations between selected parameters, particularly between zygomatic arch root diameter and articular tubercle height. Conclusion This study provides CT-based 3D morphometric reference data on osseous TMJ subunits in a European cohort. The findings indicate inter-individual morphometric variability and exploratory sex- and age-related differences in selected parameters. These data may provide anatomical reference information for future patient-specific TMJ implant research. However, the present study does not evaluate implant fit, mandibular kinematics, biomechanical performance, or clinical outcomes. Therefore, the translational relevance of these findings requires further validation.

Patient-specific alloplastic prostheses are increasingly used for reconstruction of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). This study used CT-derived three-dimensional (3D) virtual-digital surface models to analyze osseous TMJ subunits in humans and provide morphometric reference data for future patient-specific TMJ implant research.

Methods

In this retrospective exploratory study, 97 computed tomography (CT) scans from Hannover Medical School were analyzed. High-quality 3D virtual-digital models of the articulating TMJ subunits, including the mandibular condyle and glenoid fossa, were generated and used to measure relevant TMJ parameters. Parameters were compared according to sex and age, and correlation analyses were performed.

Results

Morphometric variability was observed among the osseous TMJ subunits. Men showed larger medial-lateral diameters of the mandibular condyle, greater articular tubercle height, and larger zygomatic arch root dimensions. Women showed a larger anterior-posterior diameter of the glenoid fossa. Middle-aged participants showed a larger anterior-posterior diameter of the mandibular condyle and larger sagittal dimensions of the zygomatic arch root compared with young-aged participants. Correlation analysis revealed associations between selected parameters, particularly between zygomatic arch root diameter and articular tubercle height.

Conclusion

This study provides CT-based 3D morphometric reference data on osseous TMJ subunits in a European cohort. The findings indicate inter-individual morphometric variability and exploratory sex- and age-related differences in selected parameters. These data may provide anatomical reference information for future patient-specific TMJ implant research. However, the present study does not evaluate implant fit, mandibular kinematics, biomechanical performance, or clinical outcomes. Therefore, the translational relevance of these findings requires further validation.

title: Diagnostic performance of multimodal large language models in detecting pulp stones on panoramic radiographs.
abstract: Background Pulp stones are calcified structures within the dental pulp that may increase the complexity of endodontic treatment and are commonly identified through radiographic examinations. Despite recent advances in artificial intelligence applied to dental imaging, the diagnostic capability of publicly available multimodal large language models (LLMs) for detecting pulp stones under zero-shot conditions remains unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the diagnostic performance and response consistency of multimodal LLMs in detecting pulp stones on panoramic radiographs of posterior teeth. Methods This comparative and exploratory study evaluated the GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash multimodal LLMs using panoramic radiograph image crops containing posterior teeth. A total of 64 image crops, comprising 192 posterior teeth, were analyzed. The models were tested under standardized zero-shot conditions using independent sessions and a standardized English-language prompt. Each image was submitted six times to both models to assess response consistency. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1-score with 95% confidence intervals. Intra-model consistency was assessed using majority agreement, complete agreement across repetitions, and Fleiss' Kappa coefficient. Results The models demonstrated similar overall accuracy for binary detection of pulp stones, with 56.5% for ChatGPT and 57.0% for Gemini. ChatGPT showed high specificity (96.2%) and greater intra-model stability, whereas Gemini demonstrated higher sensitivity (81.8%) and superior performance in identifying the affected tooth and dental group. However, Gemini also presented lower specificity and greater variability across repeated evaluations. Fleiss' Kappa coefficients indicated low intra-model agreement beyond chance for both models, particularly for Gemini. Conclusion Multimodal LLMs demonstrated limited capability in detecting pulp stones on panoramic radiographs, with distinct diagnostic profiles between the evaluated models. Although the findings suggest potential future applications of LLMs as auxiliary tools for dental image interpretation, their current performance does not yet support consistent clinical applicability for pulp stone detection.

title: Use of plasma chromogranin a epitopes vasostatin and catestatin as biomarkers for catecholamine-producing tumours in dogs.
abstract: Background Differentiation of catecholamine-producing tumours from other adrenal tumours remains difficult. Chromogranin A (CgA) is a marker for catecholamine secretion in the body. An assay for quantification of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin has been validated for use in dogs but not yet evaluated in dogs with catecholamine-producing tumours. The aims were to evaluate the assays foranalysis of plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin in dogs with adrenal tumours and to compare concentrations between catecholamine-producing tumours and adrenocortical tumours in dogs that were subjected to adrenalectomy. Twelve dogs with histopathologically confirmed catecholamine-secreting tumours (eleven pheochromocytomas (PCCs), one extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma (PGL)) and twelve with adrenocortical tumours were included in the study. Plasma concentrations of the CgA epitopes vasostatin and catestatin were determined byradioimmunoassay (RIA), before adrenalectomy in 23 out of 24 dogs and after adrenalectomy in six of the dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours (five PCC, one PGL). Tumour diagnosis was made by histopathology in all cases. Results Overall, median plasma concentration of the CgA epitopevasostatin in dogs with catecholamine-secreting tumours was 0.82 nmol/L (interquartile range (IQR) 0.52 to 1.60 nmol/L), which was significantly higher(Wilcoxon rank sum exact test, P= 0.0374) than the vasostatin concentration in adrenocortical tumours (median 0.50; IQR 0.34 to 0.59 nmol/L). A subsetof dogs (5/12) with catecholamine-secreting tumours had elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations preoperatively. After successful surgery, thepreoperatively elevated plasma vasostatin concentrations decreased numerically, however without reaching statistical significance. Catestatin concentrationdid not differ between tumour types. Conclusions Elevated plasma concentration of the CgA epitope vasostatin showed potential as a biomarker for asubset of catecholamine-secreting tumours.

title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows.
abstract: Background Equine colic emergencies present highly stressful, time-critical scenarios for both clinicians and patients, thus rapid and accurate diagnostic triage is paramount. To support veterinarians under these high-pressure conditions, deep learning tools can be leveraged for automated image recognition to assist in localizing abdominal organs and interpreting FLASH (Fast Localized Abdominal Sonography of Horses) ultrasound windows. Objectives A software tool was developed to identify FLASH-specific ultrasound windows on the equine abdomen and to recognize ultrasonographic organ patterns. Study design Retrospective-prospective comparison of software and clinical examination, model development. Methods A deep learning approach for image classification was used to train software to assign ultrasound images to FLASH windows. Results Strongest software performance was observed for the duodenal window, with all test images correctly classified, corresponding to a recall of 1.00. Nephrosplenic window demonstrated high classification accuracy, but 23% of images were misclassified as gastric window. While 84% of ventral images were correctly classified, 16% were predicted as duodenal window. Most pronounced confusion was observed between ventral and thoracic windows, with only 55% of thoracic images correctly identified. Left and right middle third FLASH windows 4 and 6 were substantially underrepresented and were therefore excluded from further analyses. In addition, these windows exhibited high anatomical similarity, which further complicated their differentiation. Main limitations Sources of selection bias was interpretation of windows and the definition of normal physiological ultrasound images by the examiners. The specific FLASH windows were not homogeneously dispersed in the dataset (e.g., FLASH windows 4 and 6 were underrepresented). Conclusions The developed deep learning tool demonstrates the feasibility of automated recognition of standardized equine FLASH windows and may support ultrasound training as an educational aid for first-day competencies. Future incorporation of organ-level annotations and probe position information may improve discrimination between anatomically similar windows and enhance model performance.

title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain.
abstract: Background Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients. Methods A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole. Results Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease. Conclusion Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

title: Synergistic nanotheranostic platform for fluorescence/magnetic resonance bimodal imaging-guided near infrared photoimmuno-chemodynamic thermal targeting therapy.
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) photoimmunotherapy (PIT) is a promising cancer treatment strategy involving antibody-photoabsorber conjugates. However, the imaging depth and photobleaching susceptibility of the IR700 fluorescence used for treatment monitoring are limited, and antigen heterogeneity within tumors compromises the efficacy of strictly antigen-restricted therapies. We developed a synergistic nanotheranostic platform that integrates NIR-PIT, photothermal therapy, and chemodynamic therapy (CDT) into a single MRI-visible agent (NIR-PICT 3 ). To achieve NIR-PICT 3 , conjugation of mAb-IRDye700DX (mAb-IR700) to dextran-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (nanomag-D-spio) yielded nanomag-D-spio-mAb-IR700, enabling dual imaging (IR700 fluorescence/MRI) and targeted cytotoxicity upon 690-nm irradiation. The conjugate retained antigen selectivity, exhibited activatable NIR fluorescence after cellular uptake, generated negative T1- and T2-weighted MRI contrast, and demonstrated robust, cycle-enhanced photothermal performance. Iron-mediated redox catalysis promoted ·OH generation, supporting CDT. In vivo, systemic administration led to marked tumor accumulation, as confirmed by multimodal analyses. Repeated light dosing exploited the NIR-PIT-induced super-enhanced permeability and retention (SUPR) effect, enhancing nanoparticle retention, tumor heating, and therapeutic efficacy. In EGFR+ xenografts, NIR-PICT 3 achieved superior tumor regression and survival while inducing photothermal bystander effects in antigen-heterogeneous models. These results establish a modular, image-guided strategy for platform therapy to overcome monitoring depth limitations and antigen heterogeneity in solid tumor NIR-PIT.

title: From equilibrium to dynamic metabolic imaging: the evolving role of magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging in neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract: Background Dysregulated brain metabolism is increasingly recognized to play a significant role in the development and progression of neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs). Conventional imaging methods, such as positron emission tomography (PET), are limited to assessing tracer uptake and offer no insight into its downstream metabolic fate. Additionally, PET provides no insight into dynamic metabolic fluxes and turnover, which reflect biochemical processes. In contrast, magnetic resonance spectroscopy and spectroscopic imaging MRS(I) allow non-invasive, spatially resolved in vivo investigation of specific metabolites, without the use of radioactive tracers. Main body 1 H-MRS(I) is one of the most widely utilized techniques due to its accessibility, while heteronuclear approaches, including 2 H-, 13 C-, 15 N-, and 17 O-MRS(I), broaden MRS(I)'s utility by expanding the scope of accessible metabolites. Technical and methodological advances in nuclear spin hyperpolarization-enhanced MRI further improve signal-to-noise ratio, enabling in vivo detection of low-abundance metabolites. Furthermore, revival of 2 H-MRS(I) has opened new avenues for dynamic metabolic investigation without hyperpolarization. In this review, we provide a conceptual framework for transitioning from a static to a dynamic MRS(I) approach and discuss key considerations for tracer selection, nuclear spin hyperpolarization methods, acquisition hardware, reconstruction, preprocessing, and metabolic modeling. We outline major methodological and translational challenges, including low signal-to-noise ratio, field strength, and vendor hardware variability, as well as a lack of standardization across acquisition, reconstruction, preprocessing, and modeling strategies. Conclusion Dynamic MRS(I) provides a promising foundation for in vivo brain metabolism investigation in NDDs, offering mechanistic insights into metabolic fluxes, reprogramming, and bottlenecks. Although dynamic MRS(I) is limited to a few research institutions, ongoing technical and methodological advances are improving its feasibility, biochemical specificity, and broader implementation. Standardized and harmonized acquisition, reconstruction, and preprocessing protocols are necessary to enable broad clinical implementation of these approaches. Nevertheless, the shift from static to dynamic MRS(I) has great potential to advance biomarker and diagnostic tool development, patient stratification, and longitudinal disease monitoring in NDDs, provided that current challenges and limitations are sufficiently addressed.

title: Daily image-guided carbon ion stereotactic radiotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma: paving the way for MR-guided online adaptive treatment.
abstract: Background We aim to quantify the dosimetric benefits of daily online adaptive (DOA) carbon ion stereotactic radiotherapy (CISR) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Patients and methods 13 patients received 4 × 10.5 Gy (RBE-weighted dose) CISR to 14 HCC lesions in challenging locations (N = 10: liver dome, N = 3: < 1 cm from intestines). All patients underwent daily in-room CT, with forward calculation of the baseline plan. Additionally, four patients were shuttled to a 1.5 Tesla MR scanner in treatment position for MRI simulation. Based on visual review of all data, the physician decided to treat or to perform offline plan adaptation and treat another day. We compare the dosimetry properties of four scenarios per fraction: (1) baseline plan, (2) no adaptation, (3) occasional offline adaptation (OOA), (4) DOA. Results Baseline planning target volume (PTV) and internal target volume (ITV) coverage by the prescribed dose (median coverage: PTV: 97%, ITV: 100%) significantly decreased for no adaptation (PTV: 87.6%, p = 0.0001; ITV: 97.7%, p = 0.007) and OOA (PTV: 87.8%, p = 0.0001; ITV: 97.7%, p = 0.007), while DOA maintained high PTV coverage (PTV: 95.7%, p = 0.17; ITV: 100%, p = 0.53). Frequent violations of organs-at-risk (OAR) dose constraints occurred for no adaptation and OOA (both 20/52 fractions, 38.5%). They affected the bowel, heart and esophagus up to 6 cm from the PTV. DOA led to considerably fewer (6/52 fractions, 11.5%) and less intense violations of OAR dose constraints. Conclusions Daily CT- and MR-guided CISR is feasible in the liver, and demonstrates frequent violations of initial treatment planning objectives when non-adaptive or offline adaptive approaches are followed. DOA could improve target coverage and OAR protection, while particularities of carbon ions such as overdoses far from the target should be considered.

Background

We aim to quantify the dosimetric benefits of daily online adaptive (DOA) carbon ion stereotactic radiotherapy (CISR) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

Patients and methods

13 patients received 4 × 10.5 Gy (RBE-weighted dose) CISR to 14 HCC lesions in challenging locations (N = 10: liver dome, N = 3: < 1 cm from intestines). All patients underwent daily in-room CT, with forward calculation of the baseline plan. Additionally, four patients were shuttled to a 1.5 Tesla MR scanner in treatment position for MRI simulation. Based on visual review of all data, the physician decided to treat or to perform offline plan adaptation and treat another day. We compare the dosimetry properties of four scenarios per fraction: (1) baseline plan, (2) no adaptation, (3) occasional offline adaptation (OOA), (4) DOA.

Results

Baseline planning target volume (PTV) and internal target volume (ITV) coverage by the prescribed dose (median coverage: PTV: 97%, ITV: 100%) significantly decreased for no adaptation (PTV: 87.6%, p = 0.0001; ITV: 97.7%, p = 0.007) and OOA (PTV: 87.8%, p = 0.0001; ITV: 97.7%, p = 0.007), while DOA maintained high PTV coverage (PTV: 95.7%, p = 0.17; ITV: 100%, p = 0.53). Frequent violations of organs-at-risk (OAR) dose constraints occurred for no adaptation and OOA (both 20/52 fractions, 38.5%). They affected the bowel, heart and esophagus up to 6 cm from the PTV. DOA led to considerably fewer (6/52 fractions, 11.5%) and less intense violations of OAR dose constraints.

Conclusions

Daily CT- and MR-guided CISR is feasible in the liver, and demonstrates frequent violations of initial treatment planning objectives when non-adaptive or offline adaptive approaches are followed. DOA could improve target coverage and OAR protection, while particularities of carbon ions such as overdoses far from the target should be considered.

title: Clinical utility of lung ultrasound in differentiating and monitoring complicated pediatric pneumonia: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study.
abstract: Background Lung ultrasound (LUS) is an established diagnostic tool for pediatric pneumonia, yet its utility as radiation-free alternative to computed tomography (CT) for monitoring disease progression and differentiating complicated phenotypes, specifically necrotizing pneumonia (NP) and parapneumonic effusion (PPE), has not been prospectively validated in a single comparative cohort. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and longitudinal performance of LUS, including a quantitative LUS score, in children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), CT-confirmed NP, and PPE, and to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and longitudinal performance of LUS for identifying and monitoring complicated pediatric pneumonia, including its potential as a radiation-free follow-up tool. Methods This prospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study enrolled 257 children diagnosed with CAP (n = 116), NP (n = 54), and PPE (n = 87). NP was confirmed by CT in all 54 cases; LUS was performed by trained operators at admission and on day five as a paired assessment against CT and chest radiograph findings. LUS qualitative features and quantitative scores were compared between groups and over time. Multivariable regression and ROC analysis were performed to assess diagnostic accuracy and identify predictors of clinical outcome. Results At admission, NP and PPE showed significantly higher LUS scores and more frequent absent lung sliding and heterogeneous hypoechoic consolidation than CAP (p < 0.001). A LUS score cutoff of > 8 demonstrated strong diagnostic performance at both time points (admission AUC: 0.881, sensitivity 79.02%; Day 5 AUC: 0.861, specificity 93.86%), supporting its potential role as an early screening marker and as a radiation-free bedside monitoring tool during follow-up. Longitudinal LUS assessment demonstrated significant re-aeration by Day 5 (p < 0.001), evidenced by an increased proportion of separated B-lines (35.0% to 54.9%) and a reduction in lung consolidation. On multivariable analysis, higher LUS scores independently predicted longer hospitalization on both admission (β = 0.221, p < 0.001) and Day 5 (β = 0.215, p < 0.001), and elevated D-dimer on admission (β = 0.334, p < 0.001) and Day 5 (β = 0.386, p < 0.001). Conclusion A LUS score > 8 showed promising diagnostic performance for identifying complicated pediatric pneumonia at admission and during Day 5 follow-up. Although internal bootstrap validation supported the stability of its performance, prospective validation in independent cohorts is required before implementation as a CT-sparing follow-up strategy.

title: Reproducibility and diagnostic performance of ADC for assessing response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multi-ROI comparison analysis from the phase-Ib NABUCCO trial.
abstract: Objective MRI is increasingly used to assess treatment response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), but only qualitatively. This study evaluates the reproducibility and predictive value of quantitative apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), thought to be a non-invasive surrogate for tumor cell density, in patients with MIBC receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy. Materials and methods MRI data from 35 patients, enrolled in the Phase-Ib NABUCCO trial, were analyzed. ADC maps were derived from pre- and post-treatment MRI scans. Three independent radiologists assessed multiple regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate inter-observer agreement and predictive performance for pathological complete response (pCR). ADC values were normalized using muscle tissue as a reference. Additionally, we analyzed the correlation between ADC and cell densities, derived from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) data. Results ADC measurements from the whole-tumor ROI (n = 25) demonstrated the highest reproducibility (0.98, 95% CI = [0.95-0.99]), but lacked predictive value (AUC = 0.31, 95% CI = [0.12-0.53], p = 0.109). The most hypointense ROI (n = 22) showed the strongest predictive value for pCR (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.57-1], p = 0.025), though with limited reproducibility. The difference between baseline and follow-up ADC values in the hypointense region (n = 20) again showed the highest diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.58-0.98], p = 0.015). Although muscle normalization is proposed to reduce scanner variability, it did not improve predictive performance in this cohort and occasionally reduced reproducibility. No significant correlation was found between whole-tumor ADC and cell density. Conclusion Despite analyzing different measurement techniques for ADC values, none was simultaneously reproducible and predictive, nor provided insights into the biology of the tumor. While ADC shows promise in MIBC, there is an urgent need for more standardized, robust imaging biomarkers. Key points Question Non-invasive biomarkers are urgently needed to guide bladder-preserving strategies in MIBC. Findings DWI-MRI shows promise, but standardized robust imaging biomarkers are essential for reliable response assessment. Critical relevance statement Standardized or AI-assisted ROI segmentation could improve ADC reproducibility and diagnostic accuracy in multicenter studies.

title: Practical applications of photon-counting CT in oncology: an organ-based pictorial review.
abstract: Spectral computed tomography (CT) has become an important extension of contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) in oncologic imaging by providing material-specific information beyond conventional morphologic assessment. Dual-energy CT (DECT), implemented on energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) platforms, has demonstrated the value of low-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), iodine mapping, and material decomposition for improving tumor conspicuity, delineating local extent, and supporting tissue characterization. However, broader clinical adoption of EID-CT-based DECT has been limited by increased low-keV image noise and workflow complexity. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) addresses these limitations by offering improved energy resolution, reduced electronic noise, and routine acquisition of multi-energy data without dedicated dual-energy protocols. In particular, low-keV VMI around 40 keV can be generated with clinically acceptable noise, enabling consistent enhancement-based assessment in daily practice. Iodine-based reconstructions further complement morphologic evaluation by visualizing viable tumor enhancement and enabling quantitative analysis. This organ-based pictorial review summarizes practical applications of PCD-CT-based spectral imaging in oncology. Across organ systems, spectral CT may provide complementary problem-solving information by improving lesion detection, tumor extent delineation, and diagnostic confidence, particularly when conventional CT findings are equivocal, or MRI is unavailable, contraindicated, or limited. Emerging quantitative parameters, including electron density, effective atomic number, and advanced material decomposition, may further expand oncologic CT applications, although outcome-driven validation remains limited. Together, these features position PCD-CT as a practical spectral imaging platform for routine oncologic CT. KEY POINTS: Question How can PCD-CT address low-keV image noise and workflow barriers that have limited routine DECT-based spectral imaging in oncologic CT practice? Findings PCD-CT enables low-keV VMI and iodine-based reconstructions that may improve lesion conspicuity, tumor-extent assessment, and problem-solving across organ-specific oncologic workflows. Critical relevance statement This review clarifies practical, evidence-aware uses of PCD-CT spectral reconstructions in oncology, highlighting low-keV VMI as an adjunct, selective iodine-map problem-solving, and investigational quantitative parameters.

title: The diagnostic value of high-resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI in preoperative evaluation and classification of Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome: a prospective study.
abstract: Objective Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS) is a rare female reproductive tract malformation. Accurate preoperative diagnosis and classification are vital for surgical planning. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic value of high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) T2-weighted MRI in the preoperative assessment and classification of HWWS. Materials and methods The study prospectively enrolled 84 patients clinically diagnosed with HWWS between May 2020 and January 2025. Seventy patients underwent pelvic MRI examinations, including high-resolution 3D T2 sequences (1 mm slice thickness) and conventional T2 TSE sequences, supplemented by large-field-of-view (FOV) T2 coronal imaging for urinary system evaluation and full-spine X-ray examinations for skeletal assessment. Two experienced radiologists independently evaluated the imaging features in a blinded manner, focusing on uterine morphology, obstruction sites, presence of communications, and related anomalies and complications. Consistency analysis was performed between imaging findings and surgical results in 52 surgical patients. Results Uterine morphology included: didelphys (54/70, 77.1%), complete septate (14/70, 20%), and bicornuate uterus (2/70, 2.9%). Among 52 surgical patients, 31 (59.6%) had vaginal-level obstruction with 18 (34.6%) Type I, 11 (21.2%) Type II, and 2 (3.8%) Type III, and 21 (40.4%) had cervical-level obstruction (Type IV and mixed). 3D T2 sequences identified 7 (63.6%) vaginal septum fistulas, outperforming TSE sequences, which detected none (0%) (p = 0.005). Associated findings were ipsilateral renal agenesis (98.6%), ovarian endometriosis (22.9%), hematosalpinx (22.9%), and spinal abnormalities (scoliosis (25.7%), mild scoliosis (41.4%). Conclusion High-resolution 3D T2 MRI is superior to conventional T2 TSE sequences in the preoperative evaluation of HWWS, especially for identifying communications and precisely locating obstruction sites. Key points Question Accurate preoperative structural assessment and classification of HWWS are clinically essential, yet conventional MRI has limitations in identifying fine anatomical structures and small communications. Findings High-resolution 3D T2 MRI outperforms conventional T2 TSE in identifying vaginal and cervical communications and precisely localizing obstruction sites in preoperative evaluation of HWWS. Critical relevance statement This study supports routine inclusion of 3D sequences in HWWS imaging protocols. Combined with renal and spinal assessment, it provides a comprehensive preoperative evaluation that enhances surgical planning precision and optimizes patient management strategies.

title: Contralateral-controlled thigh muscle biomarkers on CT angiography for prediction of 1-year restenosis after endovascular therapy for unilateral peripheral artery disease.
abstract: Objective To develop and internally validate a model using contralateral-controlled thigh muscle biomarkers, measured on routine computed tomography angiography (CTA), to predict clinically driven, DSA-confirmed 1-year restenosis after endovascular therapy for unilateral peripheral artery disease (PAD). Materials and methods In this retrospective cohort study, 378 patients with unilateral PAD undergoing endovascular therapy and having baseline and 1-year follow-up CTA were included. Mid-thigh skeletal muscle cross-sectional area and whole-thigh muscle volume were quantified bilaterally with semi-automated software. Contralateral-controlled biomarkers (affected minus contralateral) were derived to isolate limb-specific ischemic effects. The primary endpoint was clinically driven 1-year restenosis (≥ 50%) confirmed by DSA. Results Among 378 patients, 162 (43%) developed restenosis at a median follow-up of 12.5 months. Contralateral-controlled muscle asymmetry was independently associated with restenosis after adjustment for lesion length, baseline stenosis degree, Fontaine stage, disease duration, and TASC II classification (OR 1.43, 95% CI: 1.08-1.89, p = 0.01). Adding muscle asymmetry to a severity-only model improved discrimination from AUC 0.76 to 0.79 (DeLong p = 0.04). A baseline predictive model combining lesion length and muscle asymmetry achieved AUC 0.74; a full explanatory model incorporating longitudinal muscle changes reached AUC 0.88, with the greatest net benefit on decision curve analysis. Conclusion Thigh muscle biomarkers, acquired opportunistically from routine CTA scans, improved the prediction of 1-year restenosis after endovascular therapy and may support targeted surveillance in patients with unilateral PAD. Key points Question Can contralateral-controlled thigh muscle biomarkers on routine CT angiography improve the prediction of 1-year restenosis after endovascular therapy for unilateral peripheral artery disease? Findings In 378 PAD patients, baseline contralateral thigh muscle asymmetry independently predicted clinically driven, DSA-confirmed restenosis and improved AUC from 0.76 to 0.79. Critical relevance statement Opportunistic contralateral-controlled thigh muscle analysis on routine CT angiography provides a no-cost imaging biomarker that refines post-endovascular restenosis risk stratification, supporting targeted angiographic surveillance and advancing personalized vascular imaging practice in peripheral artery disease.

title: Myocardial work in light-chain and transthyretin-related amyloidosis with preserved ejection fraction: a cardiovascular magnetic resonance study.
abstract: Objectives To investigate pressure-volume loop (PV-loop) changes by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in cardiac amyloidosis (CA) patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and to assess PV-loop parameters' potential as subtype differential diagnostic markers. Materials and methods Between May 2017 and September 2023, 100 consecutive confirmed CA patients (14 transthyretin-related [ATTR-CA] and 86 light-chain [AL-CA]) and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were prospectively enrolled. PV-loop parameters were derived from CMR cine images and brachial blood pressure. Clinical and CMR parameters were compared between CA patients and HCs, as well as between CA subtypes. The correlations between PV-loop parameters and clinical and imaging parameters were assessed. Furthermore, the differential diagnostic performance of these PV-loop parameters was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). Bootstrapping was performed 2000 times for internal validation. Results Compared to HCs, CA patients showed significantly lower stroke work index, potential energy index (PEI), and work efficiency (all p < 0.001). AL-CA patients had higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels (2358.00 [IQR: 903.25, 5559.00] vs 810.00 [IQR: 269.00, 1136.01] pg/mL, p = 0.002) and lower PEI (0.13 [IQR: 0.07, 0.15] vs 0.15 [IQR: 0.13, 0.19] J/m², p = 0.025) than ATTR-CA patients. NT-proBNP (β = -1.94, OR = 0.14, 95% CI: 0.03-0.64, p = 0.016) and PEI (β = 0.20, OR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.07-1.44, p = 0.007) were independent predictors for AL-CA vs ATTR-CA differentiation, and combining these two parameters enhanced the diagnostic performance (bootstrapping AUC 0.847). Conclusion By providing pathophysiological insights into the distinctions between AL-CA and ATTR-CA, PV-loop parameters have the potential to serve as a complementary, contrast-free approach for differential diagnosis. Key points Question PV-loop changes by CMR in CA patients with preserved LVEF remain unknown. Objectives

To investigate pressure-volume loop (PV-loop) changes by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in cardiac amyloidosis (CA) patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and to assess PV-loop parameters' potential as subtype differential diagnostic markers.

Materials and methods

Between May 2017 and September 2023, 100 consecutive confirmed CA patients (14 transthyretin-related [ATTR-CA] and 86 light-chain [AL-CA]) and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were prospectively enrolled. PV-loop parameters were derived from CMR cine images and brachial blood pressure. Clinical and CMR parameters were compared between CA patients and HCs, as well as between CA subtypes. The correlations between PV-loop parameters and clinical and imaging parameters were assessed. Furthermore, the differential diagnostic performance of these PV-loop parameters was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). Bootstrapping was performed 2000 times for internal validation.

Results

Compared to HCs, CA patients showed significantly lower stroke work index, potential energy index (PEI), and work efficiency (all p < 0.001). AL-CA patients had higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels (2358.00 [IQR: 903.25, 5559.00] vs 810.00 [IQR: 269.00, 1136.01] pg/mL, p = 0.002) and lower PEI (0.13 [IQR: 0.07, 0.15] vs 0.15 [IQR: 0.13, 0.19] J/m², p = 0.025) than ATTR-CA patients. Conclusion

By providing pathophysiological insights into the distinctions between AL-CA and ATTR-CA, PV-loop parameters have the potential to serve as a complementary, contrast-free approach for differential diagnosis.

Key points

Question PV-loop changes by CMR in CA patients with preserved LVEF remain unknown. Findings Light-chain CA patients with preserved LVEF had higher NT-proBNP levels and lower PEI than transthyretin-related CA patients. Critical relevance statement The CMR-derived PV-loop parameters revealed pathophysiological differences between the two subtypes of CA, suggesting potential differential diagnostic value.

title: Optimizing AI-assisted decision-making in mammography screening: focusing on uncertainties.
abstract: Objective To evaluate an AI-based decision-support system for mammography interpretation, assessing its impact on diagnostic performance. Materials and methods This retrospective study analyzed 130,838 mammograms from 35,709 patients with confirmed follow-up outcomes across multiple centers, using the Digital Database for Screening Mammography (DDSM) for external validation. Representing one of the largest datasets from the Middle East, it evaluates model generalizability in underrepresented populations. An AI super-model incorporated separate UNet-based networks for lesion segmentation, a high-resolution model (4096) for calcifications, a multi-resolution ensemble (4096, 2048, 1024) for macro-scale lesions, and a risk-assessment model for malignancy prediction. Radiologists interpreted images under five scenarios: unaided, AI-assisted, AI as the final decision-maker in uncertain cases, union of radiologist and AI decisions in uncertain cases, and standalone AI. Results AI assistance significantly enhanced performance across all scenarios. Based on aggregated reader performance, AUC improved from 83.04% (95% CI: 79.8-86.3) unaided to 88.40% (95% CI: 85.6-91.2) in the union scenario (p < 0.001). Sensitivity increased from 54.8% (95% CI: 48.6-61.0) to 83.9% (95% CI: 79.3-88.4) (p < 0.001), and specificity rose from 83.6% (95% CI: 82.0-85.3) to 91.1% (95% CI: 89.8-92.4) (p < 0.001). Multi-resolution segmentation effectively detected calcifications and challenging lesions. DDSM validation confirmed model robustness. AI showed particular promise in aiding less-experienced radiologists in underserved areas to improve early cancer detection. Conclusions AI in mammography interpretation improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces uncertainty, supporting early breast cancer detection and optimized screening workflows. Key points Question Can an AI-based decision-support system improve the accuracy of mammography interpretation, reduce diagnostic uncertainty, and support less-experienced radiologists? Findings In this retrospective multicenter study, AI-assisted mammography improved sensitivity and specificity, increased cancer detection, and reduced recalls and false positives. Critical relevance statement AI integration in mammography enhances diagnostic accuracy, reduces unnecessary recalls, and supports more confident and efficient clinical decision-making, particularly by improving the performance of less-experienced radiologists in underserved and resource-limited settings where expert interpretation may be limited.
