title: Biomechanical Evaluation of Uterine Morphology and Tissue Mechanical Properties in a Computational Model of the Pelvic Cavity
abstract: Female pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a gynecological disorder characterized by pelvic organ descent that significantly impacts quality of life. With increasing global burden, approaches for early diagnosis are essential. This study illustrates a patient-specific computational model of the pelvic cavity, updating the uterine and cervical geometric model and assigning cervical tissue properties. Three distinct uterine geometric models were assembled, based on literature measurements and magnetic resonance images for comparison and validation. Human cervical properties were extrapolated from biomechanical testing of ovine pelvic tissues. Finite elements simulations of the Valsalva maneuver were conducted to analyze the biomechanical effects of varying uterine morphology and tissue properties on the pelvic cavity, including the bladder neck, vagina, and uterosacral ligaments (USLs). Results show that a uterus with softer properties assigned exhibits less vertical displacement and relies more on USLs support than a stiffer one. Furthermore, uterine volume and morphology significantly influence pelvic dynamics: a larger uterus tends toward anteversion, while a smaller uterus increases vertical vaginal displacement (10.57 mm vs 6.04 mm) and requires greater USLs support. Anatomical variations directly constrain bladder neck displacement. These computational advancements aim to enhance patient-specific modeling, assisting clinical decision-making.

title: From Manual to Machine: Development and Internal Validation of an NLP-Based Prediction Model for Brain Death Using Admission CT Reports, 2011–2024
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early identification of patients progressing toward brain death may reduce missed organ donation opportunities. We aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable natural language processing (NLP) model using admission brain computed tomog-raphy (CT) reports. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 163 adults ad-mitted between 2011 and 2024 with acute neurological injury; 96 subsequently fulfilled brain death criteria and 67 did not. Predictors were derived exclusively from admission CT report text using rule-based preprocessing and term frequency–inverse document frequency word 1–3-gram features. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine models were evaluated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 20 repetitions. Vectorization, cal-ibration, model fitting, and threshold selection were restricted to training folds. A prespecified sensitivity target of at least 95% guided threshold selection. Interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.807 (95% confidence in-terval, 0.793–0.820) and a pooled out-of-fold value of 0.791. At the high-sensitivity operating point, mean sensitivity was 0.947 and specificity was 0.275. SHAP identified clinically plausible descriptors related to cerebral edema, mass effect, ventricular distortion, ischemic injury, and midline abnormalities. CONCLUSIONS: Admission CT reports contain prognostic information that can be extracted using NLP to support earlier identification of patients at risk of progression to brain death and potential organ donation. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Study on the Value of pH-Responsive Probes in Evaluating Acidic Environment Changes During Chronic Liver Disease Progression in Rats
abstract: During the progression of chronic liver disease, changes in the acidic microenvironment of liver tissue are closely correlated with the extent of pathological injury, making precise monitoring of these changes critical for disease assessment. Traditional detection methods (e.g., blood gas analysis, tissue pH electrodes) suffer from limitations such as high invasiveness and low spatiotemporal resolution, hindering dynamic reflection of hepatic acid environment evolution. PH-responsive probes (e.g., fluorescent probes, magnetic resonance probes), leveraging their non-invasive, real-time, and high-specificity advantages, have emerged as a research focus in this field. This review focuses on the application of such probes in rat chronic liver disease models: outlining their design principles and types, analyzing their quantitative detection capabilities for liver acidification levels, summarizing their value in correlating pathological processes such as liver inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, and demonstrating their ability to identify disease progression and evaluate intervention efficacy through early detection of acidic environment changes. Studies indicate that pH-responsive probes provide a tool for elucidating the mechanisms of the acidic microenvironment in chronic liver disease and lay the foundation for developing non-invasive monitoring technologies in clinical translation, holding significant academic and practical value.

title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.

title: Binary Classification of Breast Cancer Images Using CNNs Enhanced by ALO-CLAHE-MSER Preprocessing
abstract: This work presents an intelligent image-processing framework for automatically detecting and clas-sifying benign and malignant regions in breast tissue by integrating Contrast Limited Adaptive His-togram Equalization (CLAHE), Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER), and metaheuristic opti-mization algorithms. Identifying tumor-related regions in breast images is challenging because their visual characteristics can vary considerably with tissue density, illumination conditions, surface tex-ture, intensity distribution, lesion severity, and image acquisition conditions. These variations can make conventional image segmentation and manually configured MSER approaches sensitive to pa-rameter selection and less robust when detecting heterogeneous cancerous regions. To address these limitations, this study highlights the critical role of metaheuristic optimization as a key driver for fully automating and optimizing the combined CLAHE-MSER pipeline for binary breast cancer classifica-tion. Methods: First, CLAHE is applied to the input medical images to improve local contrast and enhance visual differences between healthy and cancerous tissue. The enhanced images are subse-quently processed using the MSER technique to identify stable intensity regions potentially associated with lesions or tumor masses. Rather than relying on manual configuration, the MSER parameter space and enhancement thresholds are formulated as a multidimensional optimization problem, and metaheuristic optimization algorithms are employed to automatically explore the parameter space and determine optimal configurations for region detection. Candidate solutions are iteratively evalu-ated using an objective function designed to improve the quality, stability, spatial coherence, and ac-curacy of the detected tumor regions prior to binary classification. The proposed metaheuristic-driven CLAHE-MSER framework therefore lets the detection process adapt automatically to the visual char-acteristics of individual medical images while eliminating dependence on manually selected parame-ters. Results: We performed experimental evaluations on medical images containing healthy, benign, and malignant regions. We quantitatively evaluated the performance of the proposed CLAHE-MSER framework, optimized by metaheuristic algorithms, using several image-quality, region-detection, and binary classification metrics. The experimental results indicate that incorporating CLAHE improves local contrast and facilitates the identification of subtle differences between healthy and affected tis-sue. Furthermore, metaheuristic optimization significantly improves MSER parameter selection, re-sulting in more consistent and spatially coherent detection of tumor regions than conventional MSER configurations and non-optimized approaches. The optimized configurations better preserve relevant cancer-related structures, maximizing overall binary classification accuracy while drastically reduc-ing the detection of healthy tissue and irrelevant regions. Conclusion: Integrating CLAHE- MSER, and metaheuristic optimization provides a robust, fully automated, and adaptive framework for binary breast cancer classification based on medical image analysis. CLAHE enhances the visual infor-mation needed to distinguish affected tissue, while MSER extracts stable image regions associated with potential tumor lesions. Metaheuristic optimization serves as the central component to automate and refine the detection process by dynamically identifying suitable parameter configurations for different image conditions. The proposed methodology represents a promising computational ap-proach for automated breast cancer screening, computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), lesion classification, and intelligent medical decision support systems.

title: Predictive Value of the Cincinnati Scale for Code Stroke Activation in Relation to CT Scan Findings
abstract: Background: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide and main cause of disability in adults. Timely care is essential to achieve reperfusion and preserve brain tissue. Efforts have been made to correlate CT signs with the Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale to activate the Comprehensive Stroke Protocol. Analyzing these factors may provide useful parameters for selection. Material and Methods: This analytical, cross-sectional, observational, prospective study was conducted at the Regional General Hospital in Orizaba, Mexico. A total of 497_20 non-contrast cranial CT scans were analyzed using PACS. Patients were followed through medical records until discharge diagnosis was confirmed. Data collection occurred from March 2024_45. Results: 497_2 CT scans were reviewed. The Stroke Code was most often used in the 70-79-year age group, with 56.9% female patients. Of 72_24 ischemic stroke cases, only 24_29 were within the therapeutic window. Conclusion: The Cincinnati scale as a rapid cerebrovascular screen has only moderate to low discriminatory ability. Sensitivity and positive predictive value are very low. Therefore, it is not suitable alone. The results provide opportunity to train doctors to use the Cincinnati scale alongside the NIHSS scale, which has better predictive ability. More public education is recommended to help patients present within the window.

Efforts have been made to correlate CT signs with the Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale to activate the Comprehensive Stroke Protocol. Analyzing these factors may provide useful parameters for selection. Material and Methods: This analytical, cross-sectional, observational, prospective study was conducted at the Regional General Hospital in Orizaba, Mexico. A total of 497_20 non-contrast cranial CT scans were analyzed using PACS. Patients were followed through medical records until discharge diagnosis was confirmed. Data collection occurred from March 2024_45.

Results:

497_2 CT scans were reviewed. The Stroke Code was most often used in the 70-79-year age group, with 56.9% female patients. Of 72_24 ischemic stroke cases, only 24_29 were within the therapeutic window.

Conclusion:

The Cincinnati scale as a rapid cerebrovascular screen has only moderate to low discriminatory ability. Sensitivity and positive predictive value are very low. Therefore, it is not suitable alone. The results provide opportunity to train doctors to use the Cincinnati scale alongside the NIHSS scale, which has better predictive ability. More public education is recommended to help patients present within the window.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Investigating Pseudo-Learning and Bias Propagation in MRI Brain Tumour Classification
abstract: A brain tumour is an abnormal growth of cells in the brain, which can be either benign (noncancerous) or malignant (cancerous). The 5-year survival rate for benign brain tumours is approximately 85-95%, whereas it is only 35-36% for malignant tumours. Therefore, early detection and diagnosis of brain tumours is important. The recent developments in deep learning have allowed for high precision, accuracy, and automation in detecting these tumours, including both gliomas and pituitary tumours. In this paper, three deep learning-based models for brain tumour categorisation from MRI images are compared to understand the limitations of accuracy-based evaluation with metrics such as class-wise performance and Grad-CAM. To assess the performance and observe various behavioural issues of the models used in this analysis, the MRI scans from the Brain Tumour MRI Dataset from Kaggle and the BRISC 2025 classification dataset containing MRI images from all four major tumour groups were leveraged for their training and testing. The first model serves as a baseline EfficientNet classifier, while the second model applies fine-tuning techniques to improve feature learning. The third model further enhances performance by incorporating multi-dataset training to increase data diversity. The reported confusion matrices show that Model V3 achieved 97.63% accuracy on its 800-image test set. Because its test set differs in size and may differ in composition from those of Models V1 and V2, this result should not be interpreted as a direct like-for-like comparison.The findings highlight the importance of combining conventional performance metrics with Grad-CAM analysis when investigating model behaviour, while further evaluation is needed to establish whether multi-dataset training reduces pseudo-learning or improves generalisation.

title: Beyond 99%: Auditing Leakage, Shortcuts and Calibration in COVID-19 CT Classification
abstract: Public CT benchmarks for COVID-19 report slice-level accuracy above 99%, yet slices from one scan are near-duplicates and most datasets ship without patient IDs. We audit a MobileNetV3-Large classifier on a 19,685-slice, three-class CT dataset (non-COVID, COVID, non-informative) along four axes: leakage, shortcuts, external validity and calibration. Replacing a random slice split with a group split on recovered pseudo-patients lowers accuracy from 99.42% to 97.18%, and to 95.39% when groups follow file order. The error rate rises 4.9 to 8.0 times, and recall of COVID slices falls from 99.6% to 96.0% and 88.8%. Scalar acquisition features alone reach 0.996 balanced accuracy under a slice split and 0.630 under a group split (chance 0.333), and models trained without the lungs, or with only the lungs, both reach about 93%. On two external sites, discrimination drops (AUROC 0.83 on Sao Paulo; 0.86 for COVID lesion slices against normal patients in Tehran), and every model scores community-acquired pneumonia as more COVID-like than COVID (AUROC 0.43 to 0.49). Calibration does not transfer: binary ECE rises from 0.02 in-domain to 0.19 to 0.53 externally, and temperature scaling recovers at most 0.034. Because the main dataset has no patient IDs, we tested our grouping against true IDs on the Tehran cohort. It recovers patients poorly (adjusted Rand index at most 0.29). A nearest-neighbor probe scores 0.998 under a random slice split, 0.551 under a true patient split and 0.717 under our recovered groups, so the slice-versus-group gaps we report are lower bounds on true patient-level leakage.

title: Adult Cervical Deformity: Contemporary Evaluation, Classification, and Surgical Decision-Making.
abstract: ➢ Standing full-spine radiographs are mandatory for cervical deformity evaluation; key alignment targets include cervical sagittal vertical axis (cSVA) of ≤40 mm, T1 slope minus cervical lordosis (T1S - CL) of <15°, and a chin-brow vertical angle (CBVA) between -10° and +10° relative to the true vertical. The achievement of these thresholds is independently associated with better patient-reported outcomes, whereas values outside these ranges are associated with worse disability and quality-of-life scores.➢ The Kim-International Spine Study Group (ISSG) morphology-based classification, which identifies 4 patterns (flat neck, focal, cervicothoracic, and coronal or complex) from standing and dynamic extension radiographs, provides a reproducible morphology and flexibility-based framework that informs operative planning and has demonstrated superior interrater and intrarater reliability over prior descriptive systems; final surgical decisions integrate flexibility, neurological status, global alignment, bone quality, and patient-specific factors, and the direct impact of this classification on surgical outcomes requires further prospective validation.➢ Surgical planning is stratified by the intended lower instrumented vertebra (LIV) (Type 1: LIV T2-T4; Type 2: within the cervical spine or cervicothoracic junction; Type 3: extending past the thoracolumbar junction) and by whether the deformity is ankylosed, which determines the need for osteotomy.➢ Overall complication rates exceed 50% in prospective multicenter data; systematic risk mitigation, including neuromonitoring, tranexamic acid, staged approaches, and frailty-based patient selection, is essential for safe outcomes.➢ Despite high complication rates, the surgical correction of cervical deformity yields clinically meaningful improvements in pain and health-related quality of life at 1 year in appropriately selected patients; realistic goal-setting and individualized alignment targets are the keys to durable success.

title: Temporal Macrophage Activation Is Reduced by CCR2 Knockout in a Murine Subacromial Impingement Model.
abstract: Background Rotator cuff (RC) tendinopathy is a prevalent cause of shoulder pain and disability, yet its underlying molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Increasing evidence highlights the role of early inflammation and macrophage activation in symptom development and disease progression. C-C chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2) regulates monocyte recruitment and pro-inflammatory macrophage signaling in tendinopathy. This study characterizes the temporal inflammatory profile of RC tendinopathy and evaluates the impact of CCR2 knockout in a murine subacromial impingement (SAI) model. Methods Sixty mice (40 C57BL/6J wild type [WT SAI] and 20 CCR2 knockout [CCR2KO]) underwent bilateral placement of a subacromial surgical clip to induce RC impingement. Four additional C57BL/6J mice underwent sham surgery (WT sham controls). Animals were assessed through 42 days. Macrophage activation was quantified using microPET/CT (micro-positron emission tomography/computed tomography) and gallium-68-labeled folate receptor ligand. Selected WT SAI mice were killed at early and intermediate time points for temporal gene expression profiling. The remaining mice were killed on day 42 for histological, biomechanical, or gene expression analyses. Results WT SAI mice demonstrated a reproducible pattern of early macrophage activation, peaking on postoperative days 3 and 7. CCR2KO mice exhibited significantly reduced macrophage activation at these time points. Gene expression analysis of WT SAI supraspinatus tendons revealed early upregulation of inflammatory and M1 macrophage-related genes, followed by later increases in anti-inflammatory mediators and M2 macrophage-related markers. CCR2KO tendons demonstrated fewer tendinopathic changes on histology but did not exhibit superior biomechanical properties compared with WT SAI tendons. Conclusions RC tendinopathy exhibits a distinct early inflammatory phase characterized by macrophage activation and M1 macrophage-dominant signaling. CCR2KO reduces early inflammatory activity and may attenuate tendon degeneration. Clinical relevance Defining the inflammatory progression of RC disease may help to refine treatment strategies-particularly the use and timing of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, corticosteroid injections, and emerging biologic therapies. CCR2 represents a potential therapeutic target for modulating early inflammation and improving tendon healing.

title: Core Muscle Injury: A Combined Orthopaedic and General Surgery Algorithmic Approach for Diagnosis, Imaging, and Treatment.
abstract: » Core muscle injury (CMI) is a common cause of groin pain in athletes and reflects pathology of the inguinal canal, rectus abdominis-adductor longus (RA-AL) aponeurosis, and pubic symphysis. » There is a substantial lack of consensus on terminology and diagnostic criteria for CMI, hindering standardized evaluation, management, and research initiatives. » Diagnosis relies on structured history, physical examinations, and provocative maneuvers to identify CMI and concurrent pathology, and fluid-sensitive pelvic magnetic resonance imaging to characterize RA-AL injury. » Treatment strategies differ across sports medicine physicians, general surgeons, and orthopaedic surgeons, underscoring the need for early cross-departmental referrals to ensure all contributing pathologies are comprehensively identified and addressed. » When both adductor/RA-AL aponeurosis and inguinal canal/abdominal wall pathologies are present, prioritizing collaborative cases between orthopaedic and general surgeons is essential for decreasing operating room time, streamlining rehabilitation, and optimizing return-to-sport outcomes.

title: Proximal Scaphoid Pole Reconstruction Utilizing Ipsilateral Proximal Hamate Autograft.
abstract: Background Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented 1-4 . The use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites. Description The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program. Alternatives Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis 1,2 . These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics. Rationale The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures. Expected outcomes Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness. Important tips Limit proximal hamate resection to approximately 10 mm distal to its tip in order to replicate the scaphoid defect size while maintaining carpal stability.Ensure preservation of the triquetrohamate and volar capitohamate ligaments, as their integrity prevents instability.Rotate the graft 180° on its longitudinal axis in order to correctly orient the articular surfaces.Fixation should be rigid but not violate adjacent cartilage.Supplement with a distal radial bone graft if a distal scaphoid defect is present.Early controlled motion prevents stiffness. title: All-Suture Fixation for Acute Turf Toe Injuries.
abstract: Background Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading 1,2 . High-grade injuries may threaten return to sport and require surgery 3,4 . Here, we describe a capsular reconstruction of the great toe MTPJ with all-knotless suture anchors and suture tape augmentation for turf toe injuries, in isolation or in combination with a traumatic bunion, designed to reduce suture burden, minimize soft-tissue irritation, and facilitate recovery. Description The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor hallucis brevis insertion. Background

Turf toe is a hallux metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) injury caused by hyperextension of the great toe with axial loading1,2. High-grade injuries may threaten return to sport and require surgery3,4. Description

The procedure begins with the patient supine. A direct medial approach to the hallux MTPJ is performed. Both the medial base of the proximal phalanx and the medial eminence of the metatarsal head are drilled at isometric points, and augmentation with suture tape is then performed. Isometric drill holes are placed in the medial proximal phalanx base and metatarsal head for suture tape augmentation. A knotless suture anchor is placed approximately 3 mm proximal to the articular margin of the metatarsal head, repairing the medial capsule in a horizontal mattress fashion. An additional knotless anchor is placed at the plantar plate insertion, and the suture is passed through the tibial sesamoid sling and tensioned with the toe in 20° of plantar flexion. Suture tape is secured into the proximal phalanx with an interference screw, then passed through the deep capsule into the metatarsal head, followed by the placement of an additional interference screw into the metatarsal head. The anchor is inserted into the plantar-medial proximal phalanx at the flexor hallucis brevis insertion. The toe is flexed during tensioning, then adjusted per clinical examination and the sesamoid location beneath the metatarsal head. Knotless fixation permits incremental tensioning with intraoperative assessment of motion. Final tensioning is performed with the toe in neutral to correct deformity without overconstraint, preserving range of motion.

Alternatives

Nonoperative alternatives include rest, ice, compression and elevation; anti-inflammatory drugs; activity modification; and brief immobilization5,6. Operative alternatives include primary capsuloligamentous complex repair with nonabsorbable sutures, plantar plate advancement with bone tunnels or suture anchors if primary repair is not feasible, and concomitant procedures such as sesamoidectomy and bunionectomy based on the injury pattern2,7,8.

Suture tape augmentation resists recurrent hyperextension and valgus forces while allowing controlled physiologic motion. Knotless, low-profile suture anchors minimize bulk and hardware prominence in a region with limited soft-tissue coverage and bone stock. This construct offers a robust reconstruction option for athletes requiring predictable restoration of stability and reliable return to sport.

title: Co-occurrence of spinocerebellar ataxia type 16 and IDH-mutant oligodendroglioma associated with compound heterozygous STUB1 variants: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia type 16 (SCAR16), caused by biallelic STUB1 variants, is a rare cerebellar degenerative disorder. While STUB1 (encoding CHIP) is increasingly recognized as a tumor suppressor in gliomas, the co-occurrence of SCAR16 and intracranial glioma has not been systematically reported. This study aims to characterize the clinical, radiological, and genetic features of this unique comorbidity and explore the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Case presentation: We report a 35-year-old woman with a 7-year history of progressive gait ataxia. Initial cranial MRI revealed diffuse cerebellar atrophy. Whole-exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous STUB1 variants: a nonsense mutation (c.352C>T, p.Gln118Ter) and a missense mutation (c.433A>C, p.Lys145Gln), confirmed by familial segregation analysis. At age 33, serial MRI detected a new right temporal lobe lesion. Surgical resection was performed, and histopathology confirmed a WHO grade 2 IDH-mutant oligodendroglioma. Postoperatively, the patient received adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. Conclusions: This case provides the first clinical evidence linking biallelic STUB1 loss-of-function to both neurodegeneration and gliomagenesis. We propose a dual-pathway model wherein STUB1 deficiency impairs neuronal protein quality control (leading to cerebellar atrophy) and relieves tumor-suppressor restraint in glial cells (increasing susceptibility to IDH-mutant glioma). These findings expand the phenotypic spectrum of STUB1-related disorders and underscore the necessity of genetic screening in adult-onset ataxia with atypical features.

title: Deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognostic prediction in locally advanced cervical cancer through 18 F-FDG PET/CT and MRI combination
abstract: Abstract Background Precise pretreatment risk stratification is critical for guiding treatment intensification and personalized follow‑up in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). This study developed and validated a deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognosis prediction in patients with LACC treated with CCRT, using dual-modal pretreatment imaging from 18 F-FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI. Methods We retrospectively collected 346 patients (276 for training and 70 for testing) with LACC between June 2016 and October 2021. Radiomics and deep learning signatures were extracted from PET/CT and MRI. These signatures were integrated with the clinicopathological factors into a nomogram for clinical applications. Models were constructed using eleven machine learning algorithms, and a clinical-radiomics-deep learning model (CRDLM) was developed. The evaluation of the model’s performance was conducted through the metrics of the area under the curve (AUC). Results The CRDLM demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUCs of 0.998 (95% CI: 1.00–1.00) for training cohort and 0.901 (95% CI: 0.83–0.97) for testing cohort), which is significantly superior to conventional clinical factors (FIGO stage and SCC-Ag, AUC = 0.605–0.658). In addition, the CRDLM which combined radiomics with deep learning significantly outperformed the radiomics‑only model (AUC = 0.793, p = 0.006). Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of CRDLM reached 0.947, 0.725, and 0.786, respectively. Conclusions The CRDLM provides robust prediction of disease progression in LACC patients who received CCRT, which may facilitate personalized treatment strategies and improve clinical outcomes. Further validation in multicenter prospective studies is warranted.

title: MESO-FAP: Protocol for a Phase 1a/1b Study of [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 Radioligand Therapy Combined with Nivolumab and Ipilimumab in Advanced Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma
abstract: Abstract Background Malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) remains an aggressive malignancy associated with poor prognosis despite advances in systemic therapy. Dual immune checkpoint blockade with nivolumab and ipilimumab has improved survival outcomes and is established as a first-line treatment option for unresectable disease; however, durable responses occur in only a subset of patients, and treatment resistance remains common. Increasing evidence implicates the tumour microenvironment, particularly cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and stromal-mediated immune exclusion, as important contributors to therapeutic resistance. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), highly expressed on activated CAFs within mesothelioma stroma, represents a promising theranostic target. FAP-directed radioligand therapy using [ 177 Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 has demonstrated favourable tumour targeting and encouraging preclinical anti-tumour activity and may enhance anti-tumour immunity through modulation of the tumour microenvironment. Results MESO-FAP is an investigator-initiated multicentre phase 1a/1b study evaluating [ 177 Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab in patients with unresectable or advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma. The study comprises a dose-escalation phase using a conventional 3 + 3 design followed by a dose-expansion cohort. Eligible participants must demonstrate FAP-positive disease on screening [ 68 Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET/CT. Primary endpoints include safety, dose-limiting toxicities, determination of the maximum tolerated dose, and establishment of the recommended phase 2 dose. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include treatment response, survival outcomes, radiation dosimetry, molecular imaging biomarkers, and integrated translational analyses incorporating tissue and blood-based biomarkers. Conclusions MESO-FAP is the first prospective study investigating FAP-targeted radioligand therapy combined with dual immune checkpoint blockade in mesothelioma. The study incorporates a theranostic framework integrating molecular imaging, dosimetry, and translational biomarker analyses to establish the safety profile and recommended Phase 2 dose of stromal-directed radio-immunotherapy in MPM while generating mechanistic insights to guide future biomarker-driven clinical development. Trial registration Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR), ACTRN12626000505303. Registered 23 April 2026, https://anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=391496&isReview=true

title: Towards UASC-Net: A Pilot Study of Uncertainty-Aware 3D Brain Tumor Segmentation on BraTS 2021
abstract: Abstract Brain tumor segmentation from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a central component of treatment planning and disease monitoring, but reliable voxel-wise annotation is costly and difficult to obtain. This work presents a pilot evaluation of UASC-Net Lite v2, an uncertainty-aware extension of a compact 3D U-Net baseline for binary tumor segmentation from multimodal BraTS 2021 MRI patches. The model combines a 3D encoder–decoder segmentation pathway with attention-, prototype-, and uncertainty-related auxiliary outputs, enabling spatial confidence inspection alongside mask prediction. Experiments were conducted on a reproducible 16-case pilot subset (13 training and 3 validation cases), using 64×64×64 patches and eight training epochs. After validation-set threshold calibration, the proposed model achieved a pooled Dice score of 0.7381 and IoU of 0.5849, compared with 0.7297 and 0.5744 for the TinyUNet3D baseline. UASC-Net Lite v2 improved sensitivity from 0.7681 to 0.8609, while specificity and precision changed from 0.9685 and 0.6949 to 0.9532 and 0.6460, respectively. Qualitative visualizations show the segmentation outputs together with uncertainty and attention maps. These results should be interpreted as a pilot study rather than a full benchmark: threshold calibration was performed on the validation patches and the cohort is small. Nevertheless, the experiment provides reproducible evidence that uncertainty-aware modeling can improve lesion recall and overlap under limited-data conditions.

title: Poorly Differentiated Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Regaud–Schmincke Type of the Posterior Pharyngeal Wall: Diagnostic Challenges and Pitfalls
abstract: Abstract Background: Oropharyngeal tumors may initially present with nonspecific inflammatory symptoms, leading to diagnostic delay. Large exophytic lesions of the posterior pharyngeal wall are uncommon and may clinically and radiologically mimic infectious or inflammatory conditions. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 67-year-old male presenting with progressive dysphagia, intermittent dysphonia, and foreign body sensation in the throat. Initial clinical evaluation and histopathological examination suggested an inflammatory process. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a large polypoid mass arising from the posterior pharyngeal wall, extending to the left salpingopharyngeal fold and the hypopharynx, with craniocaudal extension of approximately 64 mm and significant airway narrowing. Repeat biopsy followed by surgical excision confirmed poorly differentiated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma of the Regaud–Schmincke type with deep soft-tissue infiltration, including invasion of striated muscle and salivary gland parenchyma. Due to impending airway obstruction, protective tracheostomy was performed prior to surgery. The postoperative course was complicated by transient acute kidney injury, which resolved with conservative management. The patient subsequently completed adjuvant external beam radiotherapy and was successfully decannulated four months postoperatively. Follow-up imaging demonstrated no evidence of local recurrence or distant metastasis. Conclusion: This case highlights the diagnostic challenges posed by exophytic oropharyngeal carcinomas presenting with inflammatory features and underscores the importance of cross-sectional imaging and repeat histopathological evaluation in patients with persistent or progressive pharyngeal symptoms.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Maternal Serum sFlt-1, PlGF, and the sFlt- 1/PlGF Ratio in Placenta Accreta Spectrum and Their Correlation With Placental Immunohistochemical Expression
abstract: Abstract Background Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is associated with substantial maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly because of severe obstetric haemorrhage. Although antenatal imaging remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, additional biomarkers may have potential value, particularly where access to advanced imaging is limited. This study evaluated maternal serum soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), placental growth factor (PlGF), and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio in women with PAS and examined their relationship with placental immunohistochemical expression. Methods This prospective case–control study was conducted at Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, in collaboration with the ICMR–National Institute of Pathology. Women with singleton pregnancies beyond 28 weeks with confirmed or clinically diagnosed PAS were enrolled as cases, while age- and gravidity-matched women undergoing caesarean delivery without PAS served as controls. Maternal plasma sFlt-1 and PlGF concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Placental tissue was evaluated by histopathology and immunohistochemistry for sFlt-1 and PlGF. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to account for baseline clinical differences. Results Sixty women were included in the final analysis, comprising 40 PAS cases and 20 controls. Median plasma sFlt-1 concentrations were lower in PAS cases than controls (23.5 vs. 29.8 ng/mL; p = 0.034), whereas PlGF concentrations were higher (270.5 vs. 48.2 pg/mL; p = 0.006). The median sFlt-1/PlGF ratio was significantly lower in PAS cases (88.1 vs. 561.1; p = 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.670 for sFlt-1, 0.716 for PlGF, and 0.753 for the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio. At the selected cut-offs, sFlt-1 showed 100% sensitivity and 65% specificity, PlGF showed 62.5% sensitivity and 100% specificity, and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio showed 62.5% sensitivity and 95% specificity. None of the three biomarkers differed significantly according to histopathological depth of invasion. In multivariable logistic regression, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio was not independently associated with PAS after adjustment for maternal age, parity, previous caesarean delivery, and previous placenta previa ( p = 0.110). Placental PlGF immunohistochemical expression showed a significant positive association with plasma PlGF concentration ( p < 0.001), whereas sFlt-1 tissue expression was uniformly weak. Conclusions Maternal plasma sFlt-1, PlGF, and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio were significantly different in women with PAS compared with controls and demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance. The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio showed the highest AUC among the biomarkers evaluated; however, it was not independently associated with PAS after adjustment for clinical factors. Plasma PlGF correlated significantly with placental PlGF immunohistochemical expression, supporting a biological relationship between circulating and placental PlGF. Larger prospective studies are required to determine whether these biomarkers can provide clinically useful adjunctive information for PAS screening and diagnosis.

title: Can Chest CT Differentiate Between Low-Risk and Higher Risk Congenital Lung Lesions in Infants?
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether chest CT can differentiate low-risk congenital lung lesions (pulmonary sequestration and CPAM type 2) from higher-risk lesions (CPAM type 1 and pleuropulmonary blastoma [PPB]) and thereby support the selection of patients for conservative management. Methods In this retrospective study (2003–2024), we identified infants with congenital lung lesions who underwent chest CT and subsequent pathologic confirmation. Two pediatric radiologists independently reviewed the anonymized CT scans, blinded to clinical and pathologic data. Lesions with a systemic arterial supply or predominant hyperinflation were classified as low risk; those with a solitary cyst, a cyst > 2 cm, or a complex cyst without systemic supply were classified as higher risk. Diagnostic confidence was graded as low, moderate, or high. Pathologic diagnosis served as the reference standard, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess interobserver agreement. Results Eighty-three children (52 male) were included. Low-risk lesions (n = 73) comprised CPAM type 2 with or without sequestration (n = 51), isolated sequestration (n = 18), and other benign lesions (n = 4). Higher-risk lesions (n = 10) included CPAM type 1 (n = 8) and type I PPB (n = 2). For moderate-to-high-confidence diagnoses, sensitivity was 100% for both radiologists; specificity was 89.2% and 93.1%; and the negative predictive value was 100%. Interobserver agreement was almost perfect (98.4%; κ = 0.95). Conclusion Chest CT enables reliable differentiation of higher-risk from low-risk congenital lung lesions and can guide the selection of candidates for conservative management.

title: Auditable Federated Learning for Multimodal Brain Tumor Classification under Label Skew and Client Dropout
abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) allows hospitals to collaboratively train deep learning models without exchanging patient images, but reported FL studies in medical imaging often assume independent and identically distributed (IID) client data and full participation in every communication round both conditions seldom hold in real clinical networks. Furthermore, although the entire premise of FL rests on the iterative averaging of client weight updates, the optimisation dynamics of those weights are rarely audited at the round level, limiting clinicians' and regulators' ability to inspect how the global model evolves under stress. This study presents an auditable federated framework for binary brain-tumour classification from a combined multimodal dataset of 4618 axial computed-tomography (CT) and 5000 magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI) slices, totalling 9618 labelled images. A lightweight three-block convolutional neural network is trained across five simulated clients using FedProx with proximal coefficient µ = 0.01 and FedAvg aggregation, under two contrasting client partitions: an IID scenario in which each client receives a balanced sample of healthy and tumour cases, and a deliberately aggressive non-IID scenario in which each client is assigned an 80% majority class. Clinically realistic stress is added by dropping a randomly chosen client in approximately 30% of rounds. At every round, for every active client, the framework records three weight summaries initial (received from the server), updated (after local training), and aggregated (new global model) together with per-client accuracy, loss, precision, recall, F1-score, communication payload, wall-clock round time, and process memory. After ten communication rounds, the global model attains 96.05% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.9641 on the held-out test set under the IID partition, and 94.96% accuracy with F1 0.9547 under the 80% label-skew non-IID partition, corresponding to an IID-to-non-IID degradation of only 1.09 percentage points despite the severe class skew and 30% per-round client dropout. Inspection of the weight-audit trace reveals a consistent and measurable shift in the output-layer mean under non-IID training that is invisible in conventional accuracy curves, suggesting that round-level weight auditing can serve as a lightweight forensic signal of distributional drift in federated medical AI.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics and Machine Learning for Predicting Refractory Outcomes in Ménière’s Disease: A Multicenter Preliminary Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the value of a machine learning model based on radiomics features derived from multicenter gadolinium-enhanced inner ear magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting refractory clinical outcomes in patients with Ménière’s disease (MD). Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients with unilateral Ménière’s disease diagnosed at two medical centers between January 2019 and December 2023. A total of 154 patients from Center 1 constituted the internal dataset and were divided into a training set (n = 123) and an internal test set (n = 31) at an 8:2 ratio, while 32 patients from Center 2 were included as an independent external validation set. According to established clinical guidelines, patients were categorized into good-control and poor-control groups. Radiomics features were extracted from the cochlea and vestibule on gadolinium-enhanced 3D-FLAIR-CUBE images, and bilateral difference (Diff) features were generated by subtracting contralateral ear features from those of the affected ear. Feature selection was performed using correlation filtering and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multiple machine learning algorithms were used to construct predictive models, which were evaluated in both internal and external datasets. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score, and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis (DCA). Results In both the training and internal test sets, the Diff radiomics model achieved higher AUCs than the symptomatic-ear radiomics models (training set: 0.815 vs. 0.682; internal test set: 0.730 vs. 0.650), along with improved sensitivity and F1 scores. Feature importance analysis indicated that vestibular-related radiomics features contributed more prominently to the prediction of refractory outcomes. Although model performance declined in the external validation set, the Diff model maintained high sensitivity (0.957) and F1 score. DCA demonstrated greater clinical net benefit of the Diff model in the training and internal test sets. Conclusion A machine learning model based on bilateral difference radiomics features can effectively predict refractory outcomes in MD and demonstrates superior performance compared with single-ear radiomics models. This approach may provide objective imaging support for prognostic assessment and individualized management of patients with MD.

title: Unintentional Weight Loss Preceding Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report and Review of Possible Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Background Unintentional weight loss is not a recognized presenting feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is more commonly associated with malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine disorders, gastrointestinal disease, or systemic inflammatory conditions. We report an unusual case in which marked involuntary weight loss preceded the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Case Presentation: A 37-year-old man presented with acute gait impairment and right lower-extremity weakness. Retrospective history revealed gradual unintentional weight loss from approximately 97 kg to 68 kg over nearly two years despite preserved appetite and the absence of gastrointestinal, infectious, endocrine, or constitutional symptoms. Extensive investigations, including laboratory testing, infectious screening, tumor markers, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasonography, and chest imaging, failed to identify an alternative cause. Neurological examination demonstrated right lower-extremity weakness, generalized hyperreflexia, bilateral pyramidal signs, and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. Brain and cervical spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple typical demyelinating lesions fulfilling the 2017 McDonald criteria for MS. The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by rituximab (1000 mg every 6 months). During four years of follow-up, the EDSS score improved from 4.0 to 1.0, MRI studies remained stable, and body weight gradually returned to two years before the start of the disease. Conclusion This case describes marked, unexplained weight loss preceding the diagnosis of RRMS, which resolved after treatment initiation and disease stabilization. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association suggests that clinically significant weight loss may represent an uncommon and underrecognized manifestation of active MS. Further studies are needed to clarify the frequency and mechanisms of weight changes in MS.

title: Transcutaneous Skin Perforation by a Protruding Xiphoid Process in a Bedbound Patient With Post-Traumatic Cervical Myelopathy: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background The xiphoid process is the smallest and most morphologically variable component of the sternum, and anterior (ventral) deviation is a recognized anatomical variant. Symptomatic xiphoid disease typically presents as localized pain (xiphodynia). Cutaneous complications are exceedingly uncommon, and only a single previous report describing an ischemic xiphisternal ulcer associated with a protruding xiphoid has been published. To the best of our knowledge, we identified no previous English-language report describing complete transcutaneous perforation of the skin by a protruding xiphoid process associated with chronic sinus formation and secondary infection. Case presentation A 71-year-old bedbound man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and post-traumatic cervical myelopathy with spastic weakness developed progressive protrusion of the xiphoid process. The angulated xiphoid tip gradually eroded through the overlying skin, producing a chronic midline ulcer with sinus tract formation and superimposed infection. Lateral radiography demonstrated marked anterior angulation of the xiphoid process with prominent ventral protrusion and irregularity of the distal tip. The patient underwent xiphoidectomy with en-bloc excision of the ulcer and debridement of devitalized soft tissue. Intraoperative culture of the resected xiphoid specimen yielded extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli, and culture-directed carbapenem therapy was administered. Histopathological examination revealed extensive ulceration with inflamed granulation tissue and a sinus tract, accompanied by reactive squamous epithelial hyperplasia (pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia), whereas the underlying bone was unremarkable and showed no evidence of malignancy. Conclusions A protruding xiphoid process can rarely progress beyond pain and superficial ulceration to cutaneous breach with sinus tract formation and secondary infection, particularly in debilitated patients with chronic immobility, diabetes mellitus, and reduced soft-tissue padding. This process appears mechanistically analogous to a pressure ulcer developing over an atypical bony prominence. Xiphoidectomy combined with debridement and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy appears to provide definitive treatment. Histopathological examination is essential because reactive pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia at the ulcer margin may mimic cutaneous malignancy.

title: Enhancing Structural Quality in Medical X-ray Super-Resolution via Domain-Aware Loss
abstract: Abstract Upscaling medical X-ray images is more challenging than enhancing natural images, because preserving accurate structural and boundary information is more important for diagnostic correctness than producing a realistic appearance. Super-resolution methods such as SRGAN, ESRGAN, and the Hybrid Attention Transformer (HAT) perform well on natural images, but when applied to medical images they can cause texture hallucination, obscure anatomical boundaries, and remove clinically important features. This study presents a comprehensive comparison of four approaches: standard SRGAN, standard ESRGAN with VGG-based perceptual loss, HAT with L1 loss, and the proposed optimised models ESRGAN_USELoss and HAT_USELoss, which incorporate a domain-specific loss function designed for X-ray imaging. The proposed USELoss (U-Net, Sobel and Edge Loss) replaces the computationally heavy VGG19 perceptual loss with a lightweight U-Net encoder that preserves multi-scale anatomical structures, and adds a Sobel-based edge loss to improve boundary accuracy, prioritising diagnostic fidelity over perceptual sharpness. On the PadChest X-ray dataset the quantitative results show large gains: standard ESRGAN reaches only 22.21 dB PSNR, whereas ESRGAN_USELoss reaches 34.04 dB, while HAT_USELoss achieves the best SSIM (0.9215) and LPIPS (0.1607). The proposed methods improve edge-preservation metrics by 5.5%, demonstrating that domain-specific loss functions are effective for clinically reliable medical image super-resolution. https://github.com/1aryantyagi/Segmentation-Paper is the Github repository of the code.

title: Double filtration plasmapheresis in anti-amphiphysin antibody syndrome mimicking multiple system atrophy: A case report
abstract: Abstract We retrospectively analyzed a patient with a positive anti-amphiphysin antibody status to characterize the clinical manifestations, diagnostic workup, and treatment results of anti-amphiphysin antibody disease that mimics multiple system atrophy (MSA), and we reviewed the relevant literature. The patient primarily presented with Parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia, and autonomic dysfunction. An 82-year-old male presented with a subacute onset of bradykinesia, ataxia, and severe orthostatic hypotension. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed hippocampal and cerebellar atrophy. Serum autoimmune neurological antibody testing was positive for anti-amphiphysin IgG (titer 1:320). Based on the multisystem involvement and exclusionary diagnostic workup, the patient was diagnosed with anti-amphiphysin antibody-associated MSA-like autoimmune neurological syndrome. After three sessions of double filtration plasmapheresis (DFPP) and sequential therapy with mycophenolate mofetil, the patient's motor function and orthostatic hypotension improved significantly. At the 6-month follow-up, the antibody titer decreased to 1:32, and the clinical condition remained stable. Anti-amphiphysin antibody syndrome can mimic MSA. Prompt neuronal autoantibody and long-term tumor screening are required for rapidly progressive atypical MSA-spectrum patients with severe autonomic failure. DFPP combined with immunosuppression achieves a favorable neurological prognosis.

title: Cephalothoracoomphalopagus Tetrabrachius Tetrapus Conjoined Twins: An Extremely Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Conjoined twins are a rare subset of monozygotic twins that usually have a poor prognosis, which has become a significant cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality. This case highlights the importance of routine antenatal care for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins. Case presentation: A 31-year-old G2P1 female in 29 4/7 weeks of gestation was referred from a primary health care center to our hospital with conjoined twins. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) ultrasonography examinations at 29 4/7 weeks of gestation revealed one fetal head accompanied by an orbital hypotelorism with an interocular diameter of 0.99 cm. The liver and heart were found to be the fusion organs involved. Polyhydramnios was observed with a maximum vertical pocket of 12.07 cm. Diagnosis of cephalo-thoraco-omphalopagus conjoined twins was made right after the first scan and consistently confirmed thereafter by six more repeated ultrasound examinations. Clinical examination after scheduled surgical delivery in 33 5/7 weeks old neonates revealed male conjoined twins with a fused head accompanied by two pairs of ears, along with a single trunk together with four neurologically independent upper limbs and lower limbs, as well as two complements of genitalia and two anuses. The twin showed signs of respiratory distress and died within one hour of birth. Conclusion Routine antenatal care and advanced ultrasound scanning are crucial for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins.

title: A novel sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) in treating intrabony defects of stage III periodontitis – Case Series
abstract: Abstract Background Sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) is a minimally invasive approach in which graft material is introduced into the intrabony defect through a pinhole made on the facial surface opposite to the intrabony defect alveolar crest and apical to the junctional epithelium 4 weeks following minimally invasive non-surgical therapy. This strategy is intended to keep the long junctional epithelium as a biologic seal over the grafted material, while providing maximum soft tissue support around the grafted material. Methods This case series presents the short-term outcome of ten patients diagnosed with stage III grade A periodontitis with interproximal intrabony defects of at least 3 mm, treated with S-PHT. Xenogenic graft material was introduced into the defect through a facial pinhole opposite to the alveolar crest following defect degranulation using minimally invasive hand and ultrasonic instrumentation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded at baseline (4 weeks after non-surgical therapy) and at 9 months following S-PHT. Results Nine months following S-PHT, all sites measured ≤ 4mm probing pocket depth (PPD). The number of sites with clinical attachment level (CAL) gain ≥ 3mm was 6 out of the 10 reported cases. Six sites out of the 10 cases fulfilled a composite outcome of pocket closure of ≤ 4 mm with ≥ 3 mm attachment gain and no bleeding on probing. Significant improvement in intrabony defect fill reported after 9 months with a mean defect fill of 3.1 mm (< 0.001). Conclusions This case series demonstrates that S-PHT, as a minimally invasive approach, could be a reliable patient friendly option for treating intrabony defects in stage III periodontitis. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov. identifiers NCT07763223 PRT-RCT-2026-001 (05-08-2026 and retrospectively registered 19-08-2026)

title: A Decade-Old Retained Intrapleural Glass Fragment in an Asymptomatic Skydiver: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Retained intrathoracic foreign bodies are usually discovered after a traumatic event that the patient clearly remembers. Glass, however, can be especially problematic. It is frequently retained, may be missed during the initial assessment, can appear variably on imaging, and may migrate months or even years after injury rather than becoming securely encapsulated. To our knowledge, an entirely asymptomatic intrapleural glass fragment discovered incidentally in a skydiver has not previously been reported. We describe a 34-year-old male skydiver who was referred after a routine screening chest radiograph showed an abnormal shadow in the right hemithorax. Ten years earlier, he had sustained a penetrating right-sided chest injury during a parachute landing, when he crashed through a window. At that time, he was treated for haemopneumothorax with intercostal drainage, but no foreign body was suspected or actively sought. On current examination, he had a contracted right hemithorax. Computed tomography revealed a radio-dense pleural foreign body. Right-sided thoracotomy was performed, and a 7 × 2.5 cm glass fragment was removed from dense pleural adhesions. His postoperative recovery was uneventful, and he later returned to skydiving.

title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
abstract: Abstract Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery. Conclusions: Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

title: Machine-Learning Models Using Multidimensional Habitats MRI Features for Assessing Recurrence and Metastasis Risk in Locally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Approximately 30%–40% of patients with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC) develop local recurrence or distant metastasis. Early identification of high-risk patients is therefore important for improving prognosis. Methods A total of 1,285 patients with LANPC from three medical centers were enrolled. Patients from center A were randomly divided into a training set (n = 693) and a validation set (n = 297) at a ratio of 7:3, while patients from centers B and C were combined as an external test set (n = 295). Ten independent machine learning models and 26 stacked ensemble models were developed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score. The incremental value of multidimensional habitat (MH) features over clinical features alone was assessed using integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), net reclassification improvement (NRI), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was used to interpret the final model. Results After recursive feature elimination (RFE), four selected clinical features, namely N category, treatment, platelet count (PLT), and smoking status, were identified and further combined with two imaging features, namely multidimensional habitats derived from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1C MH) and multidimensional habitats derived from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI MH), for model development. The stacked ensemble model combining support vector machine (SVM), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and logistic regression (LR) achieved the best overall performance, with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.761 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.719–0.798) in the 5-fold cross-validation set, 0.742 (95% CI: 0.679–0.801) in the validation set, and 0.721 (95% CI: 0.660–0.776) in the external test set. Conclusion In conclusion, the stacking model constructed based on SVM, GBM, and LR, integrating MH features and clinical features, demonstrated favorable predictive performance for recurrence and metastasis in LANPC patients, and holds promise as an effective tool for individualized risk assessment. Evidence Level: 3 Technical Efficacy: Stage 2

title: Early-onset adenocarcinoma of the ampullary rectum: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Early-onset colorectal cancer can present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, contributing to delayed diagnosis. Adenocarcinoma arising in the ampullary region of the rectum may pose additional diagnostic and surgical challenges because of its distal location. Case presentation : A 33-year-old man presented with nonspecific gastrointestinal complaints. Colonoscopy demonstrated an exophytic tumor involving the lower and middle ampullary regions of the rectum, with luminal narrowing and contact bleeding. Computed tomography showed rectal wall thickening and mesorectal lymph nodes. Histopathological examination confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (G3) with lymphovascular and perineural invasion. The final pathological stage was pT3N0M0, with no metastatic lymph nodes identified. The patient underwent abdominoperineal excision of the rectum with sigmoid colon pull-through and had an uncomplicated early postoperative course. Conclusions : This case emphasizes the need to consider colorectal malignancy in younger adults with persistent or unexplained gastrointestinal symptoms. Prompt endoscopic assessment and histopathological confirmation are essential when symptoms are atypical or persistent. Histological risk features should be integrated with tumor stage when planning postoperative management.

title: Congenital Anomalies at a Nigerian Teaching Hospital: A Retrospective Study, 2016–2018
abstract: Abstract Congenital anomalies continue to be a challenge in neonatal medicine. Improving research and the consequent improvement of prevention and management requires a forensic audit of the frequency of each anomaly in children. This retrospective study covering the years 2016–2018 was undertaken at the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) in Southern Nigeria. The findings from the 438 cases examined revealed 129 anomalies including congenital malformations of the nervous system, circulatory system, respiratory system, digestive system, genital organs/urinary system, musculoskeletal system, cleft lip and cleft palate, and chromosomal abnormalities. Talipes equinovarus, congenital malformation of the heart, and congenital cataract were the three most prevalent anomalies recorded in UCTH. The case files indicated a strong genetic predisposition for these conditions. The majority of anomalies were recorded in outpatients who only visited the hospital for delivery and had missed the benefits of managed antenatal care, where some defects may have been detected through genetic screening and ultrasound scans. The study concluded that there was a significant number of congenital anomalies within the study period.

title: Predicting high-risk HPV infection and genotype co-infection using genital tract microecological and pathogen characteristics: a machine learning study
abstract: Abstract Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions. Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract co-infections may influence HR-HPV acquisition, clearance, and persistence. However, quantitative prediction models integrating vaginal microecological indicators, genital tract pathogens, and HR-HPV genotype co-infection patterns remain limited. Methods This retrospective study included 3,403 patients who underwent concurrent HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and genital tract pathogen testing at the gynecology outpatient clinic of Hainan Women and Children’s Medical Center between January 2022 and December 2025. Of these, 765 were HR-HPV-positive and 2,638 were HR-HPV-negative. Candidate predictors were selected using univariable analysis, multicollinearity assessment based on the variance inflation factor (VIF ≦ 4), and the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine learning models were developed, and their hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with 10-fold cross-validation within the training set. Classifier chains (C ≦ C) and ensemble classifier chains (ECC) were applied to the multi-label prediction of HR-HPV genotypes. Model predictions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results In multivariable logistic regression, Ureaplasma urealyticum (UU; aOR = 2.051), Chlamydia trachomatis (CT;aOR = 1.982), severe bacterial vaginosis score (aOR = 1.614), abnormal vaginal pH (aOR = 1.375), and sialidase positivity (aOR = 1.747) were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity (all P < 0.05). The random forest model achieved the best discrimination in internal validation (AUC = 0.772, sensitivity 0.735, F1 = 0.650). For the ulti-label task, eight HR-HPV genotypes with at least 30 positive cases were included; the ECC model yielded a higher Jaccard score (0.0226) than the independent-label model (0.0190). SHAP identified UU, age, CT, and cocci abundance as leading predictors, whereas a higher Lactobacillus proportion lowered predicted risk. Conclusions Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract infections were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination, and ECC provided a modest improvement in multi-genotype prediction. These findings may inform risk-based screening, pending external validation.
